definition_zh: 违法行为；罪行；冒犯；进攻（美式拼写，英式作 offence）
definition_en: a crime or illegal act, or something that hurts or angers someone
core_image: 一张写满条款的罚单被推到当事人面前，对面的人皱起眉
scene: 社区会议上，一位居民把违规停车的照片摊在桌上，要求物业给出处理办法。 Parking without a permit is a minor offense in this district.
sceneCN: 这里 offense 指依法可罚的违法行为（第 1 个义项：可受处罚的违法行为）；句意为在本区无证停车属于轻微违法。图中可辨识物件：照片、罚单、会议桌、停车标志；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 违法行为；罪行（美式拼写）
冒犯；进攻；令人反感的事物

senses.title: A punishable illegal act
senses.definition: an act that breaks the law and can be punished
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律并可受处罚的行为
senses.example: Parking without a permit is a minor offense in this district.
senses.exampleCN: 在本区无证停车属于轻微违法。
senses.why: Latin offensa meant 'a striking against': an offence is conduct that strikes against a rule.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 offensa 意为「撞上、触犯」：违法行为就是撞上规则的行为。

senses.title: An act of insult
senses.definition: something said or done that hurts or angers another person
senses.definitionCN: 伤害或激怒他人的言行
senses.example: He took her remark as an offense and left the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把她那句话当作冒犯，离开了餐桌。
senses.why: The same image of striking against serves here: the blow lands on a person rather than on a rule.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「撞上」的形象在此落在人身上，而不是落在规则上。

senses.title: The attacking side in sport
senses.definition: the team or players whose job is to score
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中负责得分的一方或球员
senses.example: Their offense scored on the first possession.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的进攻组在第一次进攻中就得分了。
senses.why: Military attack language moved into sport, where the offense is the side that strikes.
senses.whyCN: 军事攻击的说法进入体育，那里「进攻」指负责击打的一方。

senses.title: A military attack
senses.definition: a planned attack by armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装力量有计划的攻击
senses.example: The offense began at dawn along the eastern ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 攻势在黎明沿东侧山脊开始。
senses.why: The military sense keeps the original image of a blow, aimed across a line at an enemy.
senses.whyCN: 军事义保留了「一击」的原初形象，越过界线打向敌方。

senses.title: Something repellent
senses.definition: a thing that disgusts or offends the senses
senses.definitionCN: 令感官或情感反感的事物
senses.example: The smell was an offense to everyone in the carriage.
senses.exampleCN: 那股气味让车厢里所有人都难受。
senses.why: The noun can name the source of the displeasure, not only the act that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指引起不快的行为，也能指不快本身的来源。

senses.title: A moral or religious transgression
senses.definition: a wrong considered against a moral or religious standard
senses.definitionCN: 依道德或宗教标准认定的过错
senses.example: In the old rite, the offense required a public apology.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧礼仪中，这种过失需要公开道歉。
senses.why: A moral code can be struck against just as a statute can, so the religious sense needs no courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 道德准则也会被「撞上」，正如法条会被撞上，因此宗教义不需要法庭。

senses.title: The state of being offended
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase take offense: to feel insulted
senses.definitionCN: 在「感到受辱」这一固定说法中，指被冒犯的状态
senses.example: She took offense at the question and did not answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个问题感到被冒犯，没有回答。
senses.why: The noun names not only the blow but the state of the one who received it, hence the fixed phrase for feeling insulted.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词不只指那一击，也指受击者的状态，因此有了表示「感到受辱」的固定说法。

senses.title: An attacking formation
senses.definition: the organised pattern or plan a team uses to attack
senses.definitionCN: 球队用于进攻的组织方式或计划
senses.example: The coach rebuilt the offense around two fast wings.
senses.exampleCN: 教练围绕两名快翼重建了进攻体系。
senses.why: Strategy talk turns the attacking side into a system with a name.
senses.whyCN: 战术话语把进攻方变成一个有名目的体系。

intro.en: Offense comes through Old French offense from Latin offensa 'a striking against, an injury, displeasure', from offendere, built on ob- 'against' and fendere 'to strike'. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: offense 经古法语 offense 来自拉丁 offensa「撞击、伤害、不快」，出自 offendere，由 ob-「对着」与 fendere「击打」构成，十四世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fendere meant 'to strike'; it also underlies defend, where de- adds the sense of striking away.
items.cn: fendere 意为「击打」；它也是 defend 的词根，那里 de- 增添「打回去」的意思。

items.en: Ob- 'against' plus fendere gave offendere 'to strike against, to attack, to displease'.
items.cn: ob-「对着」加 fendere 构成 offendere「撞上、攻击、使不快」。

items.en: The noun offensa named a blow, an injury and the displeasure that followed.
items.cn: 名词 offensa 指一次撞击、一处伤害，以及随之而来的不快。

items.en: Old French offense carried both the legal and the personal senses into English.
items.cn: 古法语 offense 把法律义与个人感受义一并带入英语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century offense named the attacking half of a team, borrowing the military image.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，offense 指球队的进攻一半，借用了军事意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of fendere is unsettled, so any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction; the exact first English citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：fendere 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为其提出的更古老词根都属于重构；英语最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the fendere stock, where prefixes reverse the direction of the blow; group two holds words for a breach or an insult.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 fendere 词干的词，前缀改变击打的方向；第二组是表示违法或冒犯的词。

entries.definition: The verb 'to strike against': to hurt someone's feelings or to break a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 「撞上去」的动词：伤害他人感受或违反规则。

entries.definition: De- 'away' plus fendere: to strike the blow away, hence to protect.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 fendere：把击打挡开，因此指防御。

entries.definition: The party who defends in a case; the word comes from defending, not from offending.
entries.definitionCN: 案件中作辩护的一方；这个词来自「防御」而非「冒犯」。

entries.definition: The adjective of offense, used for insults, attacks and attacking play.
entries.definitionCN: offense 的形容词，用于侮辱、攻击与进攻打法。

entries.definition: Any punishable illegal act; an offense may be minor, regulatory or military.
entries.definitionCN: 任何可罚的违法行为；offense 可以是轻微、规章性或军事性的。

entries.definition: A breaking of a specific rule or right, often administrative.
entries.definitionCN: 违反某条具体规则或权利，常属行政性质。

entries.definition: A remark that belittles a person, with no legal or military sense.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低他人的话语，不含法律或军事含义。

entries.definition: Bad conduct judged morally, which may or may not be an offense in law.
entries.definitionCN: 从道德上评判的不良行为，未必构成法律上的违法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ob- 'against' plus fendere 'strike': a blow aimed at a rule or a person.
normal.cn: ob-「对着」加 fendere「击打」：朝规则或朝人打去的一击。

normal.en: The family runs offend, offense, offensive, offender, offended.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 offend、offense、offensive、offender 与 offended。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: criminal offense, take offense, no offense.
normal.cn: 固定搭配切分义项：刑事罪行、感到被冒犯、无意冒犯。

normal.en: American spelling offense, British spelling offence; both are the same word.
normal.cn: 美式拼作 offense，英式拼作 offence，是同一个词。

normal.en: Defend uses the same root with the opposite prefix: the blow is struck away.
normal.cn: defend 用同一词根加相反前缀：把击打挡开。

abstract.en: Picture a hand striking a rulebook and then striking a person's pride.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手先打在规则手册上，又打在人的自尊上。

abstract.en: Picture a field split in two, one half pushing forward and one half holding.
abstract.cn: 想象球场分成两半，一半向前推，一半守住。

abstract.en: Picture a smell that enters a closed carriage and offends everyone in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一股气味进入密闭车厢，冒犯了里面所有人。

examples.en: The regulations list each offense and the fine attached to it.
examples.cn: 规章列出了每一项违法行为及对应的罚款。

examples.en: He apologised at once, saying he had meant no offense.
examples.cn: 他立刻道歉，说自己并无冒犯之意。

examples.en: The team's offense controlled the ball for most of the second half.
examples.cn: 该队的进攻组在下半场大部分时间控制着球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「of（对着）+ fense（打）」——对着规则或人打过去：违法、冒犯、进攻

root: 拉丁 offensa「撞击、伤害、不快」= ob-（对着）+ fendere（击打）的过去分词 offensus；fendere 更深来源不确定。英语经古法语 offense 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one blow: it lands on a rule and becomes an offence, on a person and becomes an insult, then on a scoreboard, a battlefield, the senses, a moral code, one's own pride and finally a plan for attacking.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一击：打在规则上成为违法，打在个人身上成为冒犯，再打向记分牌、战场、感官、道德准则、自己的自尊，最后成为一种进攻方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ticket pushed across a table, with the other person's brow already lowering.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张罚单被推到桌子对面，对面的人已经皱起了眉。

branches.en: THE BLOW ON A RULE: conduct strikes a statute and becomes punishable.
branches.cn: 打在规则上：行为撞上法条，因而可受处罚。

branches.en: THE BLOW ON A PERSON: the same strike lands on feelings and becomes insult.
branches.cn: 打在个人身上：同一击落在情感上，成为冒犯。

branches.en: THE ORGANISED BLOW: a team and an army both keep a side whose job is to strike.
branches.cn: 有组织的一击：球队与军队都保留负责击打的一方。

branches.en: THE SOURCE AND THE SIN: a smell can repel the senses, and a moral code can name a transgression.
branches.cn: 来源与罪过：气味能令感官反感，道德准则也能指认过失。

branches.en: ONE'S OWN STATE AND THE PLAN: a person takes offence, and a coach designs an offence.
branches.cn: 自身状态与方案：个人会感到被冒犯，教练则设计进攻方案。

intro.en: Offense is a Latin noun whose prefix and root reverse direction to build defend as well.
intro.cn: offense 是一个拉丁名词，其前缀与词根换个方向也构成 defend。

latinIntro.en: Latin fendere 'to strike' gives offend, offense and defensive words; ob- aims the blow forward, de- strikes it away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fendere「击打」衍生 offend、offense 与一批防御类词；ob- 把击打朝前送去，de- 则把它格开。

items.structure: ob- (Latin prefix, assimilated to of- before f)
items.example: The prefix aims the blow at something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把击打对准某物。

items.example: The root carries the physical blow.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着实在的一击。
这个玩笑冒犯了两名听众。

items.meaning: a blow, an injury, a breach
items.example: The offense carried a small fine.
items.exampleCN: 这项违法行为附带小额罚款。
清单列了四项违法行为。
那句话公然带有冒犯性。

items.meaning: a person who breaks the law

definition_zh: 监狱；拘留所；监禁；关进监狱
definition_en: a building where people are kept as punishment or while waiting for trial, or to put someone there
core_image: 一扇铁栅门关上，走廊尽头的灯只剩一条光
scene: 夜里的看守所走廊很安静，铁门一扇接一扇，脚步声在墙上回响。 He spent a month in jail for a traffic accident.
sceneCN: 这里 jail 是「监狱」（第 1 个义项：关押犯人或嫌疑人的场所），句意为他因一起交通事故在监狱里待了一个月。画面里的物件：铁门、走廊、灯光。

derivatives.zh: 由 jail 加 -er 构成，义为「狱卒」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「被监禁的」
由 jail 与 bird 复合，义为「常坐牢的人」

senses.title: A building for prisoners
senses.definition: a building where people are kept as punishment or while they await trial
senses.definitionCN: 关押受刑者或候审者的建筑物
senses.example: The old jail was turned into a museum.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧监狱被改成了博物馆。
senses.why: The building sense is the concrete origin, from a Roman word for a cage or prison.
senses.whyCN: 建筑义是最具体的源头，来自罗马语里表示笼子或牢房的词。

senses.title: Being imprisoned
senses.definition: the state or period of being kept in such a building
senses.definitionCN: 被关押在这种建筑里的状态或时期
senses.example: He spent three years in jail for fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 他因诈骗在狱中度过了三年。
senses.why: In jail names the state rather than the walls, so the noun shifts from building to condition.
senses.whyCN: in jail 指的不再是墙而是状态，于是名词从场所转到处境。

senses.title: To put someone in prison
senses.definition: to send someone to prison or keep them locked up
senses.definitionCN: 把某人送进监狱或锁起来
senses.example: The court jailed the driver for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 法院判这名司机入狱两年。
senses.why: The verb is the building turned into an action: put someone inside those bars.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是把那栋建筑变成动作：把人关进那些栏杆里。

senses.title: A place that feels like a prison
senses.definition: a place or situation from which someone cannot escape
senses.definitionCN: 让人无法逃脱的地方或处境
senses.example: The narrow flat felt like a jail in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那间窄公寓在夏天像座牢笼。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps bars and confinement but moves them into an ordinary room.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了栏杆与禁锢，却把它们搬进普通房间。

senses.title: A lock in a phone system
senses.definition: to remove the manufacturer's restrictions from a device
senses.definitionCN: 解除厂商对装置的锁定限制
senses.example: He tried to jail his old phone to install other software.
senses.exampleCN: 他试着给自己的旧手机越狱以安装别的软件。
senses.why: Digital use borrows the idea of breaking out of an enclosure built by someone else.
senses.whyCN: 数码用法借用了「破开别人设的围栏」这个想法。

intro.en: Jail and gaol are the same word, coming through Old French from Late Latin cavea, "cage", by way of the Vulgar Latin form caveola.
intro.cn: jail 与 gaol 是同一个词，借自诺曼法语，源自晚期拉丁语 cavea「笼子」。

items.en: cavea meant a hollow place or a cage.
items.cn: cavea 意为空腔或笼子。

items.en: cavea in medieval use meant a cage or a cell for prisoners.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语里 cavea 指令囚禁犯人用的笼子或牢房。

items.en: Old French gave the word as jaiole, also written gaiole.
items.cn: 古法语写作 jaiole，也作 gaiole。

items.en: Both spellings came into English as jail and gayhol.
items.cn: 两种拼法进入英语，成为 jail 与 gayhol。

items.en: British legal writing kept gaol for a long time, while jail won elsewhere.
items.cn: 英国法律文书长期沿用 gaol，而 jail 在其他地区流行。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jail- or gail- family; the near-meaning group holds words for prisons and locking up.
note.cn: 形近组是 jail-、gail- 词族；近义组收表示监狱与关押的词。

entries.definition: The old British spelling of jail.
entries.definitionCN: 英国旧式拼法，与本词同音同义。

entries.definition: The person who guards a jail.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「狱卒」。

entries.definition: An informal word for a prisoner who is often in jail.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「常坐牢的人」。

entries.definition: A large state building for people sentenced to long terms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「监狱」，规模更大、刑期更长。

entries.definition: One small room in a prison.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「牢房」，指单个房间。

entries.definition: The state of being kept in custody.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「拘留」，强调羁押状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the Latin cage with the double spelling jail and gaol.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁语的笼子与 jail、gaol 两种拼法连起来。

normal.en: Latin cavea meant a cage.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 cavea 意为笼子。

normal.en: Old French had both jaiole and gaiole.
normal.cn: 古法语同时有 jaiole 与 gaiole 两种写法。

normal.en: Jail and gaol are the same word.
normal.cn: jail 与 gaol 是同一个词。

normal.en: Go to jail means to be locked up.
normal.cn: go to jail 意为被关押。

normal.en: A jailer keeps the keys of the jail.
normal.cn: jailer 保管着监狱的钥匙。

abstract.en: A jail is a building made of no.
abstract.cn: 监狱是一栋由「不」砌成的建筑。

abstract.en: Bars turn space into a locked room.
abstract.cn: 铁栅把空间变成上锁的房间。

abstract.en: Any place you cannot leave feels like a jail.
abstract.cn: 任何离不开的地方都像牢笼。

examples.en: The thief was sent to jail for a year.
examples.cn: 那个小偷被判入狱一年。

examples.en: She visited her brother in jail every Sunday.
examples.cn: 她每个星期日去监狱探望哥哥。

examples.en: The police jailed two men after the robbery.
examples.cn: 抢劫案后警方把两名男子关押起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「街」—— 街尽头的铁门里就是监狱

root: 拉丁语 cavea「笼子；空腔」→ 中世纪拉丁 cavea「牢房」→ 古法语 jaiole／gaiole → 中古英语 jail／gaol。同族有 jailer、jailbird。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a prison building, the state of being inside, the act of locking up, a place that feels like a prison, and a phone unlock.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：监狱建筑、被关押状态、关进监狱的动作、像牢笼的地方，以及手机越狱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron gate closing with one thin line of light left.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁栅门关上，只留一条细细的光。

branches.en: THE MUSEUM: old cells opened to visitors.
branches.cn: 博物馆这条线：旧牢房向游客开放。

branches.en: THE YEARS: time counted behind a locked door.
branches.cn: 年月这条线：在锁着的门后数日子。

branches.en: THE COURT: a judge putting a driver inside.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：法官把司机关进去。

branches.en: THE FLAT: summer heat making a room a cage.
branches.cn: 公寓这条线：夏天把房间变成笼子。

branches.en: THE PHONE: software fences broken open.
branches.cn: 手机这条线：被打开的软件围栏。

intro.en: Jail is a French borrowing ending in -ol or -ole; English supplies the verb and person endings.
intro.cn: jail 是从法语借来的词，古式词尾是 -ol、-ole，英语补上了动词与人称词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is cavea, a cage, with few direct relatives in English spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 cavea「笼子」，英语拼写里直接同族的词不多。

definition_zh: 忠诚的；忠实的（对人、团体或事业）；忠贞的（对伴侣与誓言）；效忠的（对君主或国家）；长期支持的（顾客与读者）；矢志不渝的（对原则）；制度内批评而仍忠于整体的
definition_en: faithful to a person, group, cause or duty, and unwilling to abandon it even when doing so would be easier or more profitable
core_image: 老街照相馆的冲洗师，在师父去世、店面几经转手之后，仍每天早晨开门，把褪色的招牌擦一遍，再把师父的合影摆回柜台原位
scene: 老街上的照相馆换过三任房东，冲洗师仍每天早晨拉起卷帘门，把褪色的招牌擦干净，再把师父留下的合影摆回柜台原位。 He stayed loyal to the little studio long after its founder had died and the building had changed hands.
sceneCN: 这里 loyal 形容「对某个人或某个地方长期不离不弃的忠诚」（第 1 个义项：对某人在困境中仍不背弃）；句意为创办人去世、楼宇数次转手之后，他仍守着这间小照相馆。可辨识物件：褪色的招牌、师父的合影相框、清晨拉起的卷帘门、挂在腰间的旧钥匙；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 忠诚的；忠实的；忠贞的；效忠的；矢志不渝的

senses.title: Faithful to a person
senses.definition: staying attached to a friend, partner or leader and refusing to abandon them when loyalty becomes costly
senses.definitionCN: 对朋友、伴侣或领导者保持依恋，即使忠诚要付出代价也不离弃
senses.example: She stayed loyal to her first coach after a richer club offered her a place.
senses.exampleCN: 更有钱的俱乐部给了她一个位置之后，她仍忠于最初的教练。
senses.why: The Latin source described someone who keeps the law, and keeping faith with a person grew out of that legal idea of standing by an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源形容守法的人，而「对人守信」正是从「守着一项义务」这一法律观念里长出来的。

senses.title: Faithful to a group or cause
senses.definition: giving steady support to a team, party, school or cause over many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年间稳定地支持某个球队、党派、学校或事业
senses.example: He has been loyal to the same football club since he was six.
senses.exampleCN: 他从六岁起就忠于同一家足球俱乐部。
senses.why: The sworn bond to a lord widened into any body one chooses to belong to.
senses.whyCN: 对领主宣誓的纽带，扩展成了对任何自己选择归属的团体的纽带。

senses.title: True to a promise or duty
senses.definition: keeping the terms of an oath, a vow or a post even when no one is watching
senses.definitionCN: 即使无人监督，也遵守誓言、婚誓或职位的条款
senses.example: The nurse was loyal to her oath and never repeated what she had seen in the ward.
senses.exampleCN: 那名护士忠于自己的誓词，从未把病房里看到的事说出去。
senses.why: Medieval usage applied the lawful man to anyone who kept his word, which is the bridge from law to faithfulness.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪用法把这个「守法之人」用在任何守信者身上，这正是从法律通往忠贞的桥。

senses.title: A customer who keeps coming back
senses.definition: in business, describing a customer or reader who returns to the same shop, paper or brand year after year
senses.definitionCN: 商业用语，形容年复一年回到同一家店、同一份报纸或同一个品牌的顾客或读者
senses.example: The bookshop has a small but loyal readership that has outlasted three owners.
senses.exampleCN: 这家书店的读者不多却忠实，熬过了三任店主。
senses.why: Modern trade borrowed the moral word to measure attachment that survives better offers.
senses.whyCN: 现代商业借用了这个道德词，用来衡量那种在更优条件面前仍然留存的依恋。

senses.title: Holding to a principle
senses.definition: remaining faithful to a belief, habit or memory that one has inherited or chosen
senses.definitionCN: 对自己继承或选定的信念、习惯或记忆保持忠实
senses.example: He remained loyal to the principles his father had taught him, even when they cost him a promotion.
senses.exampleCN: 他始终忠于父亲教给他的原则，即便这些原则让他失去了升职机会。
senses.why: Once faithfulness needs no second person, it attaches to ideas, and the word describes consistency of belief.
senses.whyCN: 当忠贞不再需要另一个对象时，它就附着在观念上，这个词便描述信念的一贯。

senses.title: Faithful in love
senses.definition: remaining true to a partner and refusing the attentions of others
senses.definitionCN: 对伴侣保持忠实，拒绝他人的示好
senses.example: They promised to remain loyal to each other through two years of living in different countries.
senses.exampleCN: 他们答应在分居两国的两年里彼此忠贞。
senses.why: The oldest personal sense comes from courtly writing, where faithfulness was proved by distance and temptation.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的个人义项来自宫廷文学，那里的忠贞要靠距离与诱惑来证明。

senses.title: Sworn to a sovereign or state
senses.definition: in political and military usage, staying on the side of a crown, government or flag during conflict
senses.definitionCN: 政治与军事用语，指冲突中仍站在王室、政府或旗帜一边
senses.example: The regiment stayed loyal to the crown even after half the capital had changed sides.
senses.exampleCN: 即便半个首都都已倒向另一方，这个团仍效忠王室。
senses.why: This is the feudal core of the word: a sworn man bound to a lord by oath rather than by opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的封建内核：宣誓者靠誓言而非主张绑定于领主。

senses.title: Loyal opposition
senses.definition: in parliamentary language, describing criticism offered from inside the system by those who do not wish to overthrow it
senses.definitionCN: 议会用语，指体制内部提出批评、却不希望推翻体制的人所做的批评
senses.example: A loyal opposition attacks the minister's policy without attacking the state itself.
senses.exampleCN: 忠诚的反对派抨击部长的政策，却不攻击国家本身。
senses.why: The word can even cover sharp criticism, which shows that loyalty is owed to the whole rather than to a person's wishes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词甚至能涵盖尖锐批评，可见忠诚所向是整体，而不是某人的意愿。

intro.en: Loyal comes from Old French loial, from Latin legalis 'of the law', from lex 'law'. English legal is the same Latin word borrowed directly and much later, so loyal and legal are doublets: one source, two arrivals.
intro.cn: loyal 来自古法语 loial，源头是拉丁 legalis「法律的」，再上溯为 lex「法律」。同一个拉丁词后来又被直接借入英语，成为表示「法律的」的那个形容词，因此本词与它属同一来源的两次借入。

items.en: Lex meant law or statute. Source uncertain: no agreed origin exists, and a link with legere 'to gather, read' is a hypothesis rather than a settled derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为法律、法令。来源不确定：没有公认的起源；一般认为它与 legere「收集、读」有关，但这只是假说，不是已证实的派生。

items.en: Legalis meant 'belonging to the law'. Medieval usage also applied it to a person who keeps the law, and from there to one who keeps faith.
items.cn: legalis 意为「属于法律的」。中世纪用法也用它形容守法的人，进而形容守信的人。

items.en: Old French changed legalis into loial, and the sense moved from lawful to faithful, above all faithful to a lord.
items.cn: 古法语把 legalis 变成 loial，词义也从「合法的」转为「忠实的」，尤其指对领主忠实。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective around the fifteenth century for the bond between a sworn follower and his lord; the exact first date is not settled, and the modern senses spread outward from that bond.
items.cn: 英语大约在十五世纪借入这个形容词，用于宣誓的追随者与领主之间的纽带；确切首见年代并无定论，现代各个义项都是从那一条纽带向外扩展的。

items.en: Legalis was borrowed a second time, directly and with its meaning intact, giving English legal; the two words now share a source but not a sense.
items.cn: legalis 后来又被直接借入一次，词义保持原样，成为表示「法律的」的那个英语形容词；这两个词如今共享来源，却不共享词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the root of lex has no agreed explanation, the legere connection remains a suggestion, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：lex 的词根没有公认解释；与 legere 的关联仍只是推测；凡为其提出的印欧形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin law noun, including the doublet that arrived by the direct route, plus one look-alike from an unrelated royal stem; group two holds adjectives of attachment that differ in basis and warmth.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「法律」名词的词，包括沿直接借入路线到达的那个双重借入词，以及一个词形相近却出自无关「王室」词干的词；第二组是表示依恋的形容词，区别在于依据与温度。

entries.definition: The same Latin word borrowed directly and later: it asks what the law permits, while the adjective under study asks whom one will not abandon.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个拉丁词后来被直接借入：它问法律允许什么，而本词问的是不肯背弃谁。

entries.definition: The noun built on the same stem: it names the quality that a faithful person or act shows.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的名词：它命名的是忠实的人或行为所显现的品质。

entries.definition: It looks close and even rhymes, but it comes from Latin regalis, from rex 'king', so it shares no root with this word.
entries.definitionCN: 它词形相近甚至押韵，但来自拉丁 regalis，源于 rex「国王」，与本词不同源。

entries.definition: Built on the same law noun with a verb for carrying: it names the making of statutes and has nothing to do with devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法律名词加上表示「携带」的动词构成：它指制定法令，与忠贞无关。

entries.definition: Keeps promises and vows, especially in marriage or religion; this word adds the idea of belonging to a group or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 信守承诺与誓言，多用于婚姻或宗教；本词则多出「归属于某个团体或事业」之意。

entries.definition: Gives deep affection and time to a person or activity; it is warmer than the word under study and less about obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某活动付出深厚感情与时间；它比本词更温暖，也更少涉及义务。

entries.definition: Holds a position without wavering, often through danger or criticism; it stresses firmness rather than attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 不动摇地守住立场，常在危险或批评之中；它强调坚定，而非依恋。

entries.definition: Stays the same across years and moods; it describes steadiness of behaviour, not the bond that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 多年间、在各种情绪下都保持不变；它描述行为的一贯，而不描述产生这种一贯的纽带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real law root and its doublet, the real family built on the stem, the real fixed phrases, and the political phrase that stretches the sense furthest.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「法律」词根及其双重借入词、由同一词干长出的真实同族词、真实固定搭配，以及把这个词义拉得最远的政治说法。

normal.en: The root is the Latin word for law, and the earliest sense was the lawful man, so the adjective began as a legal description.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语中表示「法律」的词，最早的意思就是守法之人，所以这个形容词起初是一种法律描述。

normal.en: The same Latin source entered English twice: once through Old French as this word, later directly as the adjective for what the law permits.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁来源两次进入英语：一次经古法语成为本词，后来又一次直接成为表示「法律许可」的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs the noun for the quality, the adverb, the person noun, and both negative forms.
normal.cn: 同族词包括表示这种品质的名词、副词、表示效忠者的人物名词，以及两个否定形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the usual objects: a loyal friend, a loyal customer, a loyal supporter, and the frame loyal to someone.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它常接的对象：忠实的朋友、忠实的顾客、忠实的支持者，以及「忠于某人」的框架。

normal.en: The phrase loyal opposition shows that loyalty can survive open disagreement, because it is owed to the whole.
normal.cn: 「制度内忠诚的反对」这一说法表明，忠诚可以容纳公开分歧，因为它所向的是整体。

abstract.en: Picture a name carved inside a doorframe, where only the owner ever sees it.
abstract.cn: 想象门框内侧刻着一个名字，只有屋主自己看得见。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a shop nobody else bothers to open any more.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，打开一间别人都不再来开的店。

abstract.en: Picture a flag still flying over a post that the map has already forgotten.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗仍飘在地图已经遗忘的哨所上。

examples.en: The village remained loyal to its old doctor and refused to replace him with a younger one.
examples.cn: 村民始终忠于那位老医生，不肯换一位更年轻的来替代他。

examples.en: A loyal customer is worth more than a clever advertisement.
examples.cn: 一位忠实的顾客，比一则聪明的广告更有价值。

examples.en: She was loyal to the promise she had made, though no one would ever have known.
examples.cn: 她信守自己许下的承诺，尽管这件事永远不会有人知道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老友」——把你当老朋友的人，风雨里也不会走开

root: 古法语 loial ← 拉丁 legalis「法律的」← lex「法律」；lex 更深来源不确定，与 legere「收集、读」的关联仅为假说；本词与表示「法律的」的那个英语形容词，是同一拉丁词的两次借入，即双重借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a bond is chosen and then repeatedly honoured, towards a person, a group, an oath, a shop, a principle, a partner, a state, and finally towards a whole that one may criticise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个动作展开：先选定一条纽带，然后一次次守住它——对人、对团体、对誓言、对一家店、对原则、对伴侣、对国家，最后是对一个可以批评的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man still opening a shop whose founder is long dead and whose sign has faded.
core.cn: 核心意象：创办人早已去世、招牌已经褪色，那个人仍然每天来开门。

branches.en: TWO PEOPLE: friendship and romance are the same promise kept across time and distance.
branches.cn: 两个人：友情与爱情，是同一条跨过时间与距离而被守住的承诺。

branches.en: A BODY ONE BELONGS TO: a club, a party or a crown can claim the same sworn attachment.
branches.cn: 一个自己归属的集体：俱乐部、党派或王室，都能要求同一种宣誓般的归属。

branches.en: AN OBLIGATION: an oath and a principle both bind without anyone watching.
branches.cn: 一项义务：誓言与原则都在无人注视时依然约束人。

branches.en: REPEATED CHOICE: trade measures loyalty by the customer who still returns.
branches.cn: 重复的选择：商业用「顾客是否仍然回来」来衡量忠诚。

branches.en: LOYALTY THAT CRITICISES: belonging to the whole can survive disagreement with its government.
branches.cn: 会批评的忠诚：归属于整体，可以容纳与其政府之间的分歧。

intro.en: This adjective came from Old French, built on the Latin law noun; the whole family can be read through that noun and its endings.
intro.cn: 这个形容词来自古法语，建立在拉丁「法律」名词之上；整个词族都可以顺着这个名词及其词尾读出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex supplies the noun, legalis turns it into an adjective of belonging, and Old French reshaped that adjective before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lex 提供名词，legalis 把它变成表示「属于」的形容词，古法语又对这个形容词做了改造，之后英语才借入。

items.example: The root names the law that the faithful man was first said to keep.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根点出那个守法之人最初所守的法律。

items.example: The adjective turned the noun into a description of a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把名词变成了对人的描述。

items.example: Old French shifted the sense from lawful to faithful before English took the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把词义从「合法的」转为「忠实的」，之后英语才借入。

items.meaning: faithful to a person or cause
items.example: He stayed loyal to the little studio long after its founder had died.
items.exampleCN: 创办人去世很久之后，他仍忠于那间小照相馆。

items.example: The club rewarded forty years of loyalty with a single chair.
items.exampleCN: 俱乐部用一把椅子回报了四十年的忠诚。

items.example: He served loyally through three changes of owner.
items.exampleCN: 他忠实地服务，经历了三次换主。

items.meaning: one who stays faithful to a government or cause
items.example: The loyalists refused to leave the town when the government fell.
items.exampleCN: 政府倒台时，效忠者拒绝离开这座城。

items.example: A disloyal ally is more dangerous than an open enemy.
items.exampleCN: 不忠的盟友比公开的敌人更危险。

definition_en: to leave a place, especially to begin a journey, or to turn away from what is usual
core_image: 站台上一个人的背影越来越小，列车把灯光拉成一条线
scene: 车门关上，站台上的人挥手，列车慢慢滑出灯光。 The night train departs at ten.
sceneCN: 这里 depart 指「出发」（第 1 个义项：离开某地开始旅程）；句意是夜班列车十点出发。

senses.title: Leave to begin a journey
senses.definition: to leave a place in order to start a trip
senses.definitionCN: 离开某地以开始一段旅程
senses.example: The night train departs at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班列车十点出发。
senses.why: A journey begins at the moment the place is left behind.
senses.whyCN: 旅程就在把地方留在身后的那一刻开始。

senses.title: Leave a place or a post
senses.definition: to go away from a place or a position
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或某个职位走开
senses.example: She departed without a word.
senses.exampleCN: 她一句话没说就离开了。
senses.why: Not every leaving is an adventure; some are just endings.
senses.whyCN: 不是每次离开都是远行，有些只是结束。

senses.title: Turn away from a rule
senses.definition: to stop following what is usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 不再遵循通常或预期的做法
senses.example: The design departs from tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计背离了传统。
senses.why: A path that leaves the main road is also departing.
senses.whyCN: 离开大路的小径，也是一种 depart。

intro.en: Depart came through Old French departir from Latin departire, where de- means apart and partire means to divide.
intro.cn: depart 经古法语 departir 来自拉丁语 departire，其中 de- 表示分开，partire 表示划分。

items.en: Departire joined de-, meaning apart, with partire, to divide.
items.cn: departire 由 de-（分开）与 partire（划分）合成。

items.en: Departir meant to divide, to separate or to leave.
items.cn: departir 表示划分、分开或离开。

items.en: English took depart for separating and for going away.
items.cn: 英语借来 depart，既表示分开，也表示走开。

items.en: The sense of starting a journey settled in travel writing.
items.cn: 开始旅程这一层意思在游记里固定下来。

items.en: Now it also describes leaving a job or a tradition.
items.cn: 如今它也指离开一份工作或一种传统。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the depart stem, and the meaning group moves from simply leaving to setting off and pulling away.
note.cn: 形近组共用 depart 词干，近义组则从单纯离开走到动身与抽身。

entries.definition: one part of a large organization
entries.definitionCN: 大机构划分出的一个部分

entries.definition: the act of leaving a place
having recently left, or no longer living
to go away from a place
to begin a journey
to move back or leave a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a closing carriage door and end with a path that leaves the main road.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从关上的车门开始，落到一条离开大路的小径。

normal.en: De- means apart, so depart is to part from a place.
normal.cn: de- 表示分开，depart 就是与一个地方分开。

normal.en: A train departs; a passenger is left holding a ticket.
normal.cn: 列车出发了，乘客手里只剩一张票。

normal.en: Leaving a job is also a departure, even without a train.
normal.cn: 辞掉一份工作也是离开，哪怕没有列车。

normal.en: A design can depart from tradition without going anywhere.
normal.cn: 一个设计可以背离传统，却哪儿也没去。

normal.en: Depart, departure and department all begin with the same parting.
normal.cn: depart、departure 与 department 都从同一个「分开」开始。

abstract.en: Picture a platform lamp stretching into a thin line.
abstract.cn: 想象站台的灯被拉成一条细线。

abstract.en: Picture a desk cleared of everything but a key.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被清空，只剩一把钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture footprints turning off a wide road onto grass.
abstract.cn: 想象脚印从大路拐进草地。

examples.en: The night train departs at ten.
examples.cn: 夜班列车十点出发。

examples.en: She departed without a word.
examples.cn: 她一句话没说就离开了。

examples.en: The design departs from tradition.
examples.cn: 这个设计背离了传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 depart 记成「地跑」：de 像「地」，part 是分开，人从一块地上分开跑开，就是离开与出发。

root: 来自拉丁语 departire，由 de-（分开）与 partire（划分）组成，经古法语 departir 进入英语。它先表示分开与离开，十七世纪起在游记里固定为出发；现代又引申为离开职位、背离传统。

sensesIntro.en: From a train pulling out, to a person walking away, to a design leaving the old path.
sensesIntro.cn: 从开出的列车，到走开的人，再到离开旧路的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a platform lamp stretches into a line as the train pulls out.
core.cn: 核心意象：列车开走时，站台的灯被拉成一条线。

branches.en: The first sense is a journey with a time on the board.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是牌子上写着时间的旅程。

branches.en: The second sense is a person simply not there any more.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个人不再出现在那里。

branches.en: The third sense is an idea stepping off the usual road.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一个想法走下惯常的道路。

branches.en: A train and a worker can both leave on schedule.
branches.cn: 列车与工作者都能按时离开。

branches.en: Leaving a place and leaving a habit are both partings.
branches.cn: 离开一个地方与离开一种习惯，都是分别。

intro.en: Depart shares its root with departure and department, a family all about dividing and going apart.
intro.cn: depart 与 departure、department 共用词根，这一族词都关于划分与分开。

latinIntro.en: The base is partire, to divide, with de- meaning apart; the same root gives part and partial.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 partire（划分），de- 表示分开；同一个词根还给出 part 与 partial。

items.meaning: having left, or no longer living
a part of a large organization
items.example: She works in the sales department.
The departmental meeting is at nine.

items.exampleCN: 他们组成了一个跨部门团队。

items.meaning: a waiting room before a flight
items.example: We met in the departure lounge.

definition_en: in an extreme degree; very
core_image: 暴雨夜里格外昏暗的巷口路灯
scene: 雨夜的巷子里，路灯显得格外昏暗。 The alley was exceedingly dark in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 exceedingly 是「极其、格外」（第 1 个义项：达到极端的程度）；句意：雨夜的巷子里，路灯显得格外昏暗。

senses.title: To a very high degree
senses.definition: to an extremely high degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到极高的程度
senses.example: The task was exceedingly difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务极其困难。
senses.why: The adverb pushes an adjective to its extreme.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把形容词推到极端。

senses.title: Beyond what is usual
senses.definition: more than is common or expected
senses.definitionCN: 超出通常或预期
senses.example: She was exceedingly patient with the child.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个孩子格外耐心。
senses.why: Going past the usual line makes a quality stand out.
senses.whyCN: 越过通常的界线，使某种特质格外突出。

senses.title: With great care
senses.definition: in a way that goes beyond the normal effort
senses.definitionCN: 以超出寻常努力的方式
senses.example: He prepared exceedingly well for the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他为面试做了极为充分的准备。
senses.why: Effort that exceeds the norm shows in the manner.
senses.whyCN: 超出常规的努力会体现在方式上。

intro.en: Exceedingly adds -ly to exceeding, the participle of exceed.
intro.cn: exceedingly 由 exceed 的分词 exceeding 加 -ly 构成。

items.en: Excedere means to go beyond.
items.cn: excedere 意为越过。

items.en: Old French exceder carries the verb onward.
items.cn: 古法语 exceder 把动词继续传下去。

items.en: English exceed gives the participle exceeding.
items.cn: 英语 exceed 给出分词 exceeding。

items.en: The ending -ly turns it into an adverb.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把它变成副词。

items.en: Exceedingly now means extremely.
items.cn: 如今 exceedingly 意为极其。

note.en: Exceedingly strengthens a word; excessive describes too much of a thing.
note.cn: exceedingly 加强一个词，excessive 形容某物过多。

entries.definition: going beyond a limit
to be greater than
much more than is needed
to a very high degree
to a high degree
to a great degree

normalIntro.en: Exceedingly is exceeding plus -ly, pushing a word to its edge.
normalIntro.cn: exceedingly 是 exceeding 加 -ly，把一个词推到边缘。

normal.en: Exceedingly comes from exceeding.
normal.cn: exceedingly 来自 exceeding。

normal.en: It makes a strong word even stronger.
normal.cn: 它让原本强烈的词更强烈。

normal.en: Exceedingly rare means almost never seen.
normal.cn: exceedingly rare 意为几乎见不到。

normal.en: The -ly ending marks an adverb.
normal.cn: -ly 结尾标记副词。

normal.en: Avoid using it too often in speech.
normal.cn: 口语中不要过于频繁使用它。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer shooting past its top mark.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计冲过顶端的刻度。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp so bright it hurts the eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏亮得刺眼的灯。

abstract.en: Think of a road that keeps climbing past the clouds.
abstract.cn: 想象一条一直爬升到云层之上的路。

examples.en: The water was exceedingly cold.
examples.cn: 水极其寒冷。

examples.en: She is exceedingly careful with money.
examples.cn: 她花钱格外谨慎。

examples.en: The show was exceedingly popular.
examples.cn: 这场演出格外受欢迎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exceeding（超过）＋ ly」——超过一般程度，就是极其、非常。

root: exceed（超过）→ exceeding（超出的）→ exceedingly（极其），核心义「超过一般程度地」。

sensesIntro.en: Exceedingly means to an extreme degree, beyond what is usual.
sensesIntro.cn: exceedingly 意为达到极端的程度，超出寻常。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thermometer past its top mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：冲过顶端刻度的温度计。

branches.en: Going beyond the top mark is extreme.
branches.cn: 越过顶端刻度就是极端。

branches.en: Passing the usual line makes a quality stand out.
branches.cn: 越过通常的界线使特质格外突出。

branches.en: Great care shows in going beyond the norm.
branches.cn: 极为用心体现在超出常规。

branches.en: Extreme degree and unusual degree meet at the edge.
branches.cn: 极端程度与非常程度在边缘相遇。

branches.en: Both unusual quality and unusual effort exceed the norm.
branches.cn: 格外突出与格外用心都超出了常规。

intro.en: Exceedingly is exceed plus -ing and -ly.
intro.cn: exceedingly 由 exceed 加 -ing 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root cedere, to go, underlies the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cedere（走）是这一词族的基础。

items.example: Cedere appears in exceed and proceed.
items.exampleCN: cedere 出现在 exceed 与 proceed 中。

items.example: The ending makes adverbs from adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成副词。

definition_en: a person of very great ability, the ability itself, or the special spirit of something
core_image: 一位科学家在黑板上写满公式，旁人看得入神
scene: 爱因斯坦常被视为科学天才。 Einstein is often seen as a scientific genius.
sceneCN: 这里 genius 是「天才」（第 1 个义项）；句意：爱因斯坦常被视为科学天才。

senses.title: A gifted person
senses.definition: a person with very great natural ability in some field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域有非凡天赋的人
senses.example: Einstein is often seen as a scientific genius.
senses.exampleCN: 爱因斯坦常被视为科学天才。
senses.why: The word moved from a guiding spirit to a person who seems inspired.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从守护神发展为仿佛受神灵启发的人。

senses.title: Great natural ability
senses.definition: very great natural ability, especially in art or thought
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在艺术或思维方面的非凡天赋
senses.example: She has a genius for making people relax.
senses.exampleCN: 她有让人放松的天赋。
senses.why: The spirit inside a person became the talent inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 人身上的神灵，变成了人身上的才华。

senses.title: Special spirit
senses.definition: the special character or spirit that makes something work well
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物良好运转的独特气质或精神
senses.example: The genius of the plan is its simplicity.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划的精髓在于简单。
senses.why: The old guardian spirit widened to the spirit of a place or idea.
senses.whyCN: 古老的守护神含义扩展为地方或想法的精神。

intro.en: Genius first named a guardian spirit and only later named great talent.
intro.cn: genius 最初指守护神，后来才指非凡才华。

items.en: Genius was the guiding spirit of a person or place.
items.cn: genius 是人或地方的守护神。

items.en: Ingenium meant inborn talent or character.
items.cn: ingenium 意为天生的才能或性情。

items.en: English kept the sense of a tutelary spirit.
items.cn: 英语保留了守护神的含义。

items.en: It came to mean exceptional natural ability.
items.cn: 它逐渐指出众的天赋。

items.en: It also came to mean a person who has such ability.
items.cn: 它也开始指拥有这种才能的人。

note.en: Genius is compared with look-alike words and words for great ability.
note.cn: 把 genius 与形近词以及表示非凡才能的词作比较。

entries.definition: a spirit in old stories that grants wishes
entries.definitionCN: 故事中实现愿望的精灵

entries.definition: real and not false
willing to give more than expected
a natural ability to do something well
a special natural ability
a young person with extraordinary ability

normalIntro.en: Genius is the talent that seems to come from somewhere beyond the person.
normalIntro.cn: genius 就是仿佛来自人本身之外的天赋。

normal.en: Einstein is often seen as a scientific genius.
normal.cn: 爱因斯坦常被视为科学天才。

normal.en: She has a genius for making people relax.
normal.cn: 她有让人放松的天赋。

normal.en: The genius of the plan is its simplicity.
normal.cn: 这个计划的精髓在于简单。

normal.en: The idea was a stroke of genius.
normal.cn: 这个主意是神来之笔。

normal.en: He was a man of genius and patience.
normal.cn: 他是个既有天才又有耐心的人。

abstract.en: Genius is patience wearing its best clothes.
abstract.cn: 天才是穿上最好衣服的耐心。

abstract.en: The spirit that guides a hand is older than the hand.
abstract.cn: 指引一只手的灵感，比手本身更古老。

abstract.en: Every mind has a quiet room where new things are made.
abstract.cn: 每颗心都有一间安静的房间，新事物在那里被造出来。

examples.en: Einstein is often seen as a scientific genius.
examples.cn: 爱因斯坦常被视为科学天才。

examples.en: She has a genius for making people relax.
examples.cn: 她有让人放松的天赋。

examples.en: The idea was a stroke of genius.
examples.cn: 这个主意是神来之笔。

dict_mnemonic.text: genius 与 genie（精灵）同源：古人相信每个人身边都有一位守护精灵，被精灵眷顾的人就拥有非凡才能，于是 genius 从「精灵」变成了「天才」。

root: 来自拉丁语 genius（守护神），与 ingenium（天赋）同源，核心义从「附身的神灵」发展为「非凡才能」。

sensesIntro.en: Genius means a person of great ability, that ability itself, or the special spirit of a thing.
sensesIntro.cn: genius 意为才能出众的人、这种才能本身，或事物的独特精神。

core.en: An extraordinary power that seems to guide the mind.
core.cn: 一种仿佛在引导头脑的非凡力量。

branches.en: A room full of people watches one thinker.
branches.cn: 满屋子的人注视着一位思考者。

branches.en: A hand finds the right note without searching.
branches.cn: 一只手不用寻找就找到了正确的音符。

branches.en: A simple rule makes a whole system work.
branches.cn: 一条简单的规则让整个系统运转起来。

branches.en: The person and the gift are often named by one word.
branches.cn: 人和天赋常常被同一个词命名。

branches.en: Talent in a mind and spirit in a plan both look effortless.
branches.cn: 头脑中的才华与计划中的精神，看起来都毫不费力。

intro.en: Genius belongs to a Latin family of inborn talent and guiding spirit.
intro.cn: genius 属于拉丁语中表示天赋与守护神的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin genius meant a guardian spirit; ingenium meant inborn talent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 genius 意为守护神，ingenium 意为天生的才能。

items.exampleCN: 这个孩子很早就显露了天赋。

items.meaning: more than one person of great ability
items.example: The lab attracted geniuses from many countries.
items.exampleCN: 这个实验室吸引了来自许多国家的天才。
她想出了一个巧妙的解决办法。

items.meaning: the quality of being clever and inventive
items.exampleCN: 这个装置显示出极大的独创性。

items.example: The genie rose from the lamp.
He had a genius-like grasp of numbers.
items.exampleCN: 他对数字有天才般的把握。

items.example: The toy is admired for its ingeniousness.
items.exampleCN: 这个玩具因精巧而受到赞赏。

latinEntries.example: Genius watched over a person from birth.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 守护神从出生起就看护着一个人。

latinEntries.example: Ingenium is the source of ingenious.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ingenium 是 ingenious 的来源。

definition_en: to amuse people, to receive guests, or to keep an idea in mind
core_image: 主人张开双臂把客人迎进屋，让他们坐下、吃喝、笑出声
scene: 晚饭后爷爷讲了一个长笑话，把孩子们逗得直笑。 Grandpa told a long joke after dinner and entertained the children for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 entertain 是「使娱乐」（第 1 个义项：让人开心消遣）；句意：晚饭后爷爷讲了一个长笑话，逗得孩子们笑了一个小时。

senses.title: To amuse and hold attention
senses.definition: to give people pleasure and keep them interested
senses.definitionCN: 给人快乐并让他们保持兴趣
senses.example: The clown entertained the crowd for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 小丑逗了观众一个小时。
senses.why: The old sense of holding someone is applied to holding their attention pleasantly.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「留住某人」之意，被用来表示愉快地留住他们的注意力。

senses.title: To receive guests
senses.definition: to welcome guests and provide food, drink, or company
senses.definitionCN: 迎接客人并提供饮食或陪伴
senses.example: They entertained friends at home all weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 整个周末他们都在家招待朋友。
senses.why: Hospitality is the oldest social sense: keeping people together in your house.
senses.whyCN: 待客是最古老的社交义项：把人们留在自己家里相聚。

senses.title: To hold an idea in mind
senses.definition: to consider or keep an idea, hope, or doubt in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在心里考虑或保留某种想法、希望或疑虑
senses.example: He refused to entertain the idea of moving abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝考虑移居国外的想法。
senses.why: The mind is pictured as a host that can receive and hold a thought.
senses.whyCN: 心智被想象成一位可以接纳并留住想法的主人。

intro.en: Entertain comes from Old French entretenir, to hold together or maintain, from entre, between, and tenir, to hold.
intro.cn: entertain 来自古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持），由 entre（之间）与 tenir（握住）构成。

items.en: Tenere means to hold or keep.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、保持。

items.en: Tenir continues the Latin verb for holding.
items.cn: tenir 延续拉丁语中表示「握住」的动词。

items.en: Entretenir means to hold together and keep up.
items.cn: entretenir 意为使相聚、维持。

items.en: Middle English entretinen means to keep up or maintain.
items.cn: 中古英语 entretinen 意为维持、保持。

items.en: The sense of amusing guests and audiences becomes common.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，招待客人、娱乐观众的意思流行起来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the amusement, hospitality, and mental senses together.
items.cn: 现代英语把娱乐、招待与心中怀有三个义项并存。

note.en: Entertain is a holding verb, and it sits near its own family and near words for amusing and hosting.
note.cn: entertain 是一个「留住」动词，与自身词族以及表示逗乐和待客的词相邻。

entries.definition: shows or activities that amuse people
a person who amuses an audience
amusing and enjoyable
to make someone laugh or smile
to receive and look after guests
to keep a thought or feeling in mind

normalIntro.en: Entertain goes back to French tenir, to hold: it holds a guest's attention and keeps it.
normalIntro.cn: entertain 可追溯到法语 tenir（握住）：它把客人的注意力握住并留住。

normal.en: Enter- means between, and tenir means hold: to hold someone in a pleasant state.
normal.cn: enter- 表示之间，tenir 表示握住：把某人留在愉快的状态里。

normal.en: Entertain guests is the older hospitality sense.
normal.cn: entertain guests 是更古老的待客义项。

normal.en: Entertain an idea is to hold it in the mind for a while.
normal.cn: entertain an idea 是把想法在心里留一会儿。

normal.en: Entertainment is the noun, and entertainer is the person.
normal.cn: entertainment 是名词，entertainer 是人。

normal.en: Compare amuse: amuse makes people laugh, while entertain can also mean to host.
normal.cn: 对比 amuse：amuse 让人发笑，而 entertain 还可表示招待。

abstract.en: Picture a host holding open the door while plates are passed around.
abstract.cn: 想象主人扶着门，盘子在客人之间传递。

abstract.en: Imagine a juggler keeping five balls in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象杂耍者让五个球停在空中。

abstract.en: Think of a thought held lightly in the palm before it is accepted.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法被轻轻托在掌心，尚未被接受。

examples.en: The clown entertained the crowd for an hour.
examples.cn: 小丑逗了观众一个小时。

examples.en: They entertained friends at home all weekend.
examples.cn: 整个周末他们都在家招待朋友。

examples.en: He refused to entertain the idea of moving abroad.
examples.cn: 他拒绝考虑移居国外的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enter + ten」——把客人请进门，再用十成的热情留住他，就是招待与娱乐；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住）→ 古法语 entretenir（维持、使相聚）→ 中古英语 entretinen → 现代英语 entertain，由「留住、维持」引申为招待与娱乐。

sensesIntro.en: The verb first means to keep something together, then to keep guests, then to keep attention amused, and finally to keep an idea in mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词先表示「维持在一起」，再表示留住客人，继而表示留住注意力使人开心，最后表示把想法留在心里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: guests held in a warm circle of food, talk, and laughter.
core.cn: 核心意象：客人被留在饮食、交谈与笑声组成的温暖圈子里。

branches.en: Amusing people is holding their attention pleasantly.
branches.cn: 逗人开心，就是愉快地留住注意力。

branches.en: Hospitality keeps guests physically and socially close.
branches.cn: 待客让客人在身体与社交上保持亲近。

branches.en: Holding an idea keeps it in the mind as a guest.
branches.cn: 怀有想法，就是把它当作客人留在心里。

branches.en: A good host both feeds guests and keeps them amused.
branches.cn: 好主人既招待饮食，也让客人开心。

branches.en: Receiving people and receiving ideas both use the same holding image.
branches.cn: 接纳人与接纳想法使用同一个「留住」意象。

intro.en: Entertain is a French verb rebuilt on a Latin root, and English endings carry it into noun and adjective forms.
intro.cn: entertain 是建立在拉丁词根上的法语动词，英语词尾把它扩展到名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere means to hold, and French entretenir means to hold together or keep up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 表示握住，法语 entretenir 表示使相聚、维持。

items.exampleCN: entre- 出现在 entretenir 开头。

items.example: Inter is the Latin source of entre-.
items.exampleCN: inter 是 entre- 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Tenere is the deep root of tenir.
items.exampleCN: tenere 是 tenir 的深层词根。

items.example: Entretenir joins the prefix and the verb.
items.exampleCN: entretenir 把前缀与动词结合。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

items.example: Entertainment is what the verb produces.
items.exampleCN: entertainment 是动词产生的结果。

items.example: Entertainer names the person on stage.
items.exampleCN: entertainer 指舞台上的那个人。

definition_en: a person who is in charge of a group of soldiers or of a military operation
core_image: 站在队列最前方，肩上扛着全队责任的那个人
scene: 舰桥上，他对着地图下达最后的指令。 The commander ordered his troops to hold the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 commander 指「指挥官」（第 1 个义项：部队的负责人）；句意是指挥官命令部队守住大桥。

senses.title: A military leader
senses.definition: an officer who leads soldiers or directs a military operation
senses.definitionCN: 率领士兵或指挥军事行动的军官
senses.example: The commander gave the order to withdraw.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥官下达了撤退的命令。
senses.why: The ending -er marks the person who does what the base verb names.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 标记出执行词基动作的那个人。

senses.title: A naval rank
senses.definition: a rank in the navy between lieutenant commander and captain
senses.definitionCN: 海军中位于少校与上校之间的军衔

senses.title: Head of a police unit

intro.en: Commander is command plus -er, the ending for the person who performs an act.
intro.cn: commander 由 command 加 -er 构成，词尾表示执行动作的人。

items.en: Mandare meant to entrust a task to someone.
items.cn: mandare 意为把任务托付给某人。

items.en: Commandare carried the sense of giving orders.
items.cn: commandare 带上了下达命令的意思。

items.en: Old French comandeor named the one who gives orders.
items.cn: 古法语 comandeor 指下命令的那个人。

items.en: English commander first meant a leader of armed men.
items.cn: 英语 commander 最初指武装人员的首领。

items.en: It became a formal rank in armies and navies.
items.cn: 它在陆军与海军中成为正式军衔。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same command stem, while the meaning group names leaders of groups.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在同一 command 词干上的词，近义组列出带领队伍的各类首领。

entries.definition: a soldier trained for sudden raids
a rule given with authority
to praise someone formally
a person who holds a position of command
a person who guides a group
the head of a group or organization

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one person giving orders, then move to the rank and to police units that use the same title.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个人下命令开始，再走到军衔与沿用同一称呼的警队。

normal.en: Commander is command plus -er, so it is the person, not the order.
normal.cn: commander 是 command 加 -er，指人而不指命令。

normal.en: A commander in chief stands above every other commander.
normal.cn: 总司令站在所有其他指挥官之上。

normal.en: In the navy the word is a rank, not just a job.
normal.cn: 在海军里这个词是军衔，不只是职务。

normal.en: The plural commanders simply adds s.
normal.cn: 复数 commanders 只加一个 s。

normal.en: Wherever people must be led, someone takes the title.
normal.cn: 凡是有队伍需要带领的地方，就有人接过这个称呼。

abstract.en: Picture a figure on a bridge looking down at a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身影站在舰桥上俯视地图。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers turning as one at a raised hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起，一列士兵同时转身。

abstract.en: Picture a room of reporters waiting for one short statement.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子记者等着一段简短声明。

examples.en: The commander ordered his troops to hold the bridge.
examples.cn: 指挥官命令部队守住大桥。

examples.en: A good commander listens before giving orders.
examples.cn: 好的指挥官先倾听，再下令。

examples.en: The commanders met to plan the next move.
examples.cn: 各位指挥官会面商定下一步行动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commander 记成 command（命令）加 er（人）：下命令的那个人，就是指挥官。

root: 由 command 加表人的后缀 -er 构成，词根上溯拉丁语 mandare（托付）与 commandare（下令），本义是下达命令的人。

sensesIntro.en: From the person who leads troops, to a fixed naval rank, and finally to the head of a police division.
sensesIntro.cn: 从带领部队的人，到固定的海军军衔，再到警区主管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the figure at the front of a line, carrying the whole group's responsibility.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在队列最前方，肩上扛着全队责任的那个人。

branches.en: Leading soldiers is the original and broadest sense.
branches.cn: 率领士兵是最初也最宽泛的义项。

branches.en: A navy turned the title into a rank with a badge.
branches.cn: 海军把这个称呼变成带标识的军衔。

branches.en: Police forces borrowed the word for a division head.
branches.cn: 警队借用这个词来称呼警区主管。

branches.en: The same word names a role and a grade at once.
branches.cn: 同一个词同时指职务与等级。

branches.en: Army and police share the idea of one person answerable for many.
branches.cn: 军队与警队共享一个观念：一人为众人负责。

intro.en: Commander is a derived agent noun, and its wider family comes from the base command.
intro.cn: commander 是派生的施动名词，更大的家族来自词基 command。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mandare, to entrust, links commander with mandate and demand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mandare（托付）把 commander 与 mandate、demand 连在一起。

items.example: The commanders shared one radio channel.

definition_en: violent and dangerous, very strong in force, or very intense in feeling or competition
core_image: 铁笼里的猛兽压低身子，喉咙里滚出低吼
scene: 笼中的猛兽压低身子，喉咙里滚出低吼。 The fierce animal refused to back away.

senses.title: Violent animal
senses.definition: violent and dangerous, especially of an animal
senses.definitionCN: 凶猛危险，尤指动物
senses.example: The fierce animal refused to back away.
senses.exampleCN: 那只凶猛的野兽不肯后退。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of dangerous aggression.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示危险攻击性的基本义。

senses.title: Very strong in force
senses.definition: very strong in force or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 力量或强度非常大
senses.example: A fierce storm hit the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 一场猛烈风暴袭击了海岸。
senses.why: Weather and forces can be fierce.
senses.whyCN: 天气与自然力量都可以是猛烈的。

senses.title: Intense in feeling
senses.definition: very intense in competition, debate, or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争、辩论或情感上非常激烈
senses.example: The teams fought a fierce battle for the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 两队为奖杯展开了激烈争夺。
senses.why: The word extends from physical force to emotion.
senses.whyCN: 该词从物理力量延伸到情感强度。

intro.en: Fierce comes from Old French fers or fier, from Latin ferus, wild.
intro.cn: fierce 源自古法语 fers 或 fier，出自拉丁语 ferus（野性的）。

items.en: Ferus meant wild or untamed.
items.cn: ferus 意为野性的、未驯服的。

items.en: Ferox described a savage animal.
items.cn: ferox 形容凶猛的野兽。

items.en: Fers and fier carried the sense of proud and savage.
items.cn: fers 与 fier 兼具高傲与凶猛之意。

items.en: English fiers meant fierce or proud.
items.cn: 英语 fiers 意为凶猛的或骄傲的。

items.en: Fierce also described storms and competition.
items.cn: fierce 也用来形容风暴与竞争。

note.en: Fierce is compared with similar-looking words and with words for intensity.
note.cn: 把 fierce 与形近词以及表示强烈的词作比较。

entries.definition: to make a hole through something
in a violent or intense way
the quality of being fierce
savage and cruel
using great force
very great or strong

normalIntro.en: Fierce means violent in force, whether in an animal, a storm, or a contest.
normalIntro.cn: fierce 意为力量凶暴，无论动物、风暴还是竞赛。

normal.en: A fierce dog guards the gate.
normal.cn: 一只凶猛的狗守着大门。

normal.en: Fierce competition means rivals push hard.
normal.cn: fierce competition 指对手拼得很凶。

normal.en: The wind grew fierce at night.
normal.cn: 夜里风变得猛烈。

normal.en: The adverb is fiercely.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 fiercely。

normal.en: Fierce shares a root with ferocious.
normal.cn: fierce 与 ferocious 同根。

abstract.en: What is fierce cannot be ignored.
abstract.cn: 凶猛之物无法被忽视。

abstract.en: Intensity makes a small thing fill the room.
abstract.cn: 强度能让小东西充满整个房间。

abstract.en: Fierce loyalty can be as dangerous as fierce anger.
abstract.cn: 激烈的忠诚可以和激烈的愤怒一样危险。

branches.en: An animal ready to attack.
branches.cn: 随时准备攻击的动物。

branches.en: A contest pushed to the limit.

definition_zh: 亲密的；私人的；精深的；密友
definition_en: very close and personal, private, or known in great detail
core_image: 两个人坐在离得很近的沙发上，说话轻到只有对方听得见
scene: 冬夜的厨房里，两个人并肩坐着，声音压得很低，说着不在人前讲的事。 They shared an intimate meal at the back of the restaurant.
sceneCN: 这里 intimate 是「亲密的」（第 1 个义项：关系十分亲近），句意为他们在餐馆后部一起吃了一顿亲切的饭。画面里的物件：小桌、两把椅子、低垂的灯。

pos.zh: 形容词：亲密的；私人的；精深的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -cy 构成，义为「亲密；私密」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「亲密地；密切地」
由动词义加 -ion 构成，义为「暗示；通告」

senses.title: Very close as people
senses.definition: having a close personal relationship marked by warmth and trust
senses.definitionCN: 拥有以温暖与信任为标志的亲近私人关系
senses.example: Only her most intimate friends knew the news.
senses.exampleCN: 只有她最亲密的朋友知道这个消息。
senses.why: Latin intimus was the superlative of inward, so intimate means the innermost.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intimus 是「向内」的最高级，所以 intimate 就是「最里面的」。

senses.title: Private and personal
senses.definition: concerning very private matters of body, feeling, or home life
senses.definitionCN: 涉及身体、情感或家庭生活中极为私密之事的
senses.example: The diary records intimate thoughts she never published.
senses.exampleCN: 日记记下了她从未发表的私密想法。
senses.why: What is innermost is also least public, so closeness slips into privacy.
senses.whyCN: 最里面的也最不公开，于是「亲近」滑向「私密」。

senses.title: Deep and detailed
senses.definition: showing a thorough, detailed understanding of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 显示出对某主题透彻而细致的理解
senses.example: He has an intimate knowledge of the city's old streets.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这座城的老街了如指掌。
senses.why: Knowledge too can be intimate: you know a thing down to its inside.
senses.whyCN: 知识也可以是亲密的：你一直知道它的内里。

senses.title: A close friend
senses.definition: a person with whom one is on very close terms
senses.definitionCN: 与之关系极为亲近的人
senses.example: He invited a few intimates to the small ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他只请了几位密友参加那场小型仪式。
senses.why: The adjective turned noun names the people who belong to one's innermost circle.
senses.whyCN: 形容词作名词，指属于你内圈的那些人。

senses.title: To hint at
senses.definition: to make something known indirectly rather than stating it
senses.definitionCN: 不直说而间接让人知道某事
senses.example: She intimated that the decision was already made.
senses.exampleCN: 她暗示决定其实已经作出。
senses.why: A separate Latin verb intimare, to announce, gave this sense through the same shape.
senses.whyCN: 另一个拉丁动词 intimare 意为「宣告」，经由同一形式带来这一义项。

intro.en: Intimate comes from Latin intimus, the innermost, plus a separate verb intimare, to announce.
intro.cn: intimate 来自拉丁语 intimus「最里面的」，并另有一个动词 intimare「宣告」。

items.en: Intimus was the superlative of inward things.
items.cn: intimus 是表示「向内」一类的最高级。

items.en: Intimare meant to bring something inside, then to announce it.
items.cn: intimare 意为把某事带入内部，后引申为宣告。

items.en: Intimatus described a very close friend.
items.cn: intimatus 描述极为亲近的朋友。

items.en: English took intimate for close friendship and private matters.
items.cn: 英语用 intimate 指亲密友谊与私密之事。

items.en: Later usage added detailed knowledge and the verb of hinting.
items.cn: 后来的用法又添上「精深了解」与「暗示」的动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the intim- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for closeness.
note.cn: 形近组共用 intim- 词干；近义组收表示亲近的词。

entries.definition: The state of being close and private.

To frighten someone into doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「恐吓」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: Near in space or in feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「靠近的；亲近的」。

entries.definition: Well known from frequent contact.

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold on to the innermost idea inside the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住词里「最里面」这个念头。

normal.en: Intimate comes from intimus, the superlative of inward.
normal.cn: intimate 出自 intimus，即「向内」的最高级。

normal.en: Intimate friends are the ones inside the circle, not at its edge.

normal.en: Intimate details belong inside four walls.

normal.cn: 别和 intimidate 混：那个词讲的是害怕。

normal.en: To intimate is to say something without quite saying it.
normal.cn: to intimate 是话没说透就已经让人明白。

abstract.en: Intimacy is a small room built inside a large world.
abstract.cn: 亲密是在大世界里隔出的一间小屋。

abstract.en: The word means the innermost layer of a life.
abstract.cn: 这个词指人生最里面的一层。

abstract.en: Privacy is the price and the proof of closeness.
abstract.cn: 私密既是亲近的代价，也是它的证明。

examples.en: The two families have been intimate for three generations.
examples.cn: 这两家三代以来一直来往亲密。

examples.en: The small hall makes the concert feel intimate.
examples.cn: 小音乐厅让这场音乐会听来很亲切。

examples.en: He intimated that he would not stand again.
examples.cn: 他暗示自己不会再参选。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: close as people, private, deeply detailed, a close friend, and to hint.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people on a sofa, voices lowered to a whisper.

branches.en: THE CIRCLE: friends admitted to the inner ring.

normalIntro.en: The forehead is the fore part of the head, where thought and worry show.
normalIntro.cn: forehead 是头的前部，也是思考与忧虑显现的地方。

normal.en: She has a broad forehead.
normal.cn: 她的前额很宽。

normal.en: He wiped his forehead.
normal.cn: 他擦了擦额头。

normal.en: A kiss on the forehead is gentle.
normal.cn: 亲吻额头是温柔的动作。

normal.en: His forehead wrinkled in thought.
normal.cn: 他思考时额头起了皱。

normal.en: The child pressed his forehead to the glass.
normal.cn: 孩子把额头贴在玻璃上。

abstract.en: The forehead carries the weight of thought.
abstract.cn: 额头承载着思考的重量。

abstract.en: Worry writes its lines on the forehead.
abstract.cn: 忧虑把纹路写在额头上。

abstract.en: A forehead is a silent diary.
abstract.cn: 额头是一本无声的日记。

examples.en: She touched his forehead gently.
examples.cn: 她轻轻碰了碰他的前额。

examples.en: His forehead was lined with worry.
examples.cn: 他的额头因忧虑起了皱纹。

examples.en: Sweat ran down his forehead.
examples.cn: 汗水顺着他的额部流下。

dict_mnemonic.text: forehead 就是 fore（前）加 head（头）：头的前部，就是额头。

root: 源自古英语 forheafod，由 fore（在前）与 head（头）复合，核心义「头的前部」。

sensesIntro.en: Forehead means the part above the eyes, the place where emotion shows, or the hairline area.
sensesIntro.cn: forehead 意为前额、显露情绪的额头或靠近发际的额部。

core.en: The front and top part of the face.
core.cn: 脸的前上部。

branches.en: The flat area above the eyes.
branches.cn: 眼睛上方的平坦区域。

branches.en: Worry leaves lines there.
branches.cn: 忧虑在那里留下纹路。

branches.en: Sweat runs down near the hair.
branches.cn: 汗水在发际附近流下。

branches.en: Body and feeling share one word.
branches.cn: 身体与情感共用一个词。

branches.en: The same surface is named by its edges.
branches.cn: 同一表面也可按边缘来指称。

intro.en: Forehead forms a small family of face-shape words.
intro.cn: forehead 形成一个表示面部形状的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Forehead has no Latin ancestor; Latin frons, forehead, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: forehead 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 frons（前额）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: having a forehead of a kind

items.example: The portrait shows a high-foreheaded man.
items.exampleCN: 画像中是一位前额高的男子。

items.example: A forehead line deepened as he frowned.

items.meaning: a gentle kiss on the forehead
items.example: The mother gave him a forehead kiss.

items.meaning: a device that reads temperature at the forehead
items.example: The nurse used a forehead thermometer.
A red mark sat at mid-forehead.

definition_zh: 复杂精密的；老练世故的；老于世故的人
definition_en: complex and refined, or a person with much worldly experience
core_image: 一位衣着讲究的行家端详着一件精密仪器
scene: 他在艺术方面是个老练世故的人。 He is a sophisticate in matters of art.
sceneCN: 这里 sophisticate 是「老于世故的人」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他在艺术方面是个老练世故的人。

senses.title: Complex and precise
senses.definition: highly developed and complex in design
senses.definitionCN: 设计上高度发达、复杂的
senses.example: The lab uses sophisticate equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验室使用精密设备。
senses.why: The old sense of mixed or adulterated turned into finely made.
senses.whyCN: 原本「掺混、复杂」的含义变成了「制作精细」。

senses.title: A worldly expert
senses.definition: a person with a lot of experience of the world and its ways
senses.definitionCN: 对世情有丰富经验的人
senses.example: He is a sophisticate in matters of art.
senses.exampleCN: 他在艺术方面是个老练世故的人。
senses.why: A person of refined knowledge is a person of the world.
senses.whyCN: 知识精致的人，就是通达世情的人。

senses.title: Refined and elegant
senses.definition: showing refined and elegant taste
senses.definitionCN: 表现出高雅精致的品味
senses.example: The room has a sophisticate elegance.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有一种高雅的格调。
senses.why: Complexity in taste becomes elegance.
senses.whyCN: 品味上的复杂变成了优雅。

intro.en: Sophisticate goes back to the Greek word for a wise man.
intro.cn: sophisticate 可追溯到希腊语中表示智者、行家的词。

items.en: Sophos meant wise or skilled.
items.cn: sophos 意为智慧的或熟练的。

items.en: Sophistes named an expert or a teacher of wisdom.
items.cn: sophistes 指行家或智者之师。

items.en: Sophisticus meant relating to the sophists.
items.cn: sophisticus 意为与智者派有关的。

items.en: Sophisticare meant to adulterate or make complex.
items.cn: sophisticare 意为掺假或使复杂。

items.en: English used the word for refined and worldly things.
items.cn: 英语用这个词形容精致复杂、通达世情的事物。

note.en: Sophisticate is compared with look-alike words and words for refined complexity.
note.cn: 把 sophisticate 与形近词以及表示精致复杂的词作比较。

entries.definition: complex, refined, or worldly
the quality of being refined or complex
a second-year student
having many connected parts
polished and elegant
experienced in life and its ways

normalIntro.en: A sophisticate is a person whose knowledge has many layers.
normalIntro.cn: sophisticate 指知识有很多层的人。

normal.en: He is a sophisticate in matters of art.
normal.cn: 他在艺术方面是个老练世故的人。

normal.en: The lab uses sophisticate equipment.
normal.cn: 这个实验室使用精密设备。

normal.en: The room has a sophisticate elegance.
normal.cn: 这个房间有一种高雅的格调。

normal.en: The design is sophisticate but simple to use.
normal.cn: 这个设计很精密，但使用简单。

normal.en: She spoke to a sophisticate audience.
normal.cn: 她向一群见多识广的听众讲话。

abstract.en: Sophistication is simplicity that has learned many lessons.
abstract.cn: 精致，是学会了很多功课的简单。

abstract.en: The worldly person still keeps one simple question.
abstract.cn: 通达世情的人，仍会保留一个简单的问题。

abstract.en: Complexity is not wisdom until it can be explained.
abstract.cn: 复杂如果不能被解释清楚，就还不是智慧。

examples.en: He is a sophisticate in matters of art.
examples.cn: 他在艺术方面是个老练世故的人。

examples.en: The lab uses sophisticate equipment.
examples.cn: 这个实验室使用精密设备。

examples.en: She spoke to a sophisticate audience.
examples.cn: 她向一群见多识广的听众讲话。

dict_mnemonic.text: sophisticate 与 sophisticated（复杂的、老练的）同源，来自希腊语 sophos（智慧）：知识层次多的人就是「老练世故的人」，设计层次多的东西就是「精密复杂的」。

root: 来自希腊语 sophos（智慧）经 sophistes（行家）进入拉丁语，核心义「有层层知识的、精致复杂的」。

sensesIntro.en: Sophisticate means complex and precise, a worldly expert, or refined and elegant.
sensesIntro.cn: sophisticate 意为复杂精密、老于世故的人，或高雅精致的。

core.en: Knowledge with many layers.
core.cn: 有许多层的知识。

branches.en: A machine with countless precise parts.
branches.cn: 一台有无数精密零件的机器。

branches.en: A collector reads a painting at a glance.
branches.cn: 收藏家一眼就读懂一幅画。

branches.en: A quiet room shows perfect proportion.
branches.cn: 一间安静的房间呈现出完美的比例。

branches.en: Precision in machines and taste in rooms both take work.
branches.cn: 机器的精密与房间的品味都需要工夫。

branches.en: The expert mind understands complex things simply.
branches.cn: 行家的头脑能把复杂之事看得简单。

intro.en: Sophisticate belongs to a Greek family of wisdom and refinement.
intro.cn: sophisticate 属于希腊语中表示智慧与精致的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sophisticus and sophisticare carried the word into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sophisticus 与 sophisticare 把这个词带入英语。

items.exampleCN: 这个精致的设计让他们满意。
这家俱乐部吸引老练世故的人。
这个系统显示出高度的复杂精巧。

items.example: The process is sophisticating the design.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程正在让设计变得更复杂。

items.example: The meal was plain and unsophisticated.

definition_en: belonging to a navy or its warships, or connected with war at sea
core_image: 灰色军舰的舰首切开浪头，甲板上一排水兵抬手敬礼
scene: 港口外的海面灰蒙蒙的，一排军舰挂着旗，贴着水线缓缓出港。 A naval exercise was held off the coast last month.
sceneCN: 这里 naval 是「海军的」（第 1 个义项：属于海军）；句意为上个月在近海举行了一场海军演习。图中可辨识物件：军舰、舰旗、海面。

derivatives.zh: 与 naval 同出拉丁语 navis（船）的同源词，义为「海军；舰队」
同出 navis（船），由 navis 与 agere（驾驶）合成，义为「航行；导航」
由 navigate 加 -ion 构成，义为「航行；航海术」

senses.title: Belonging to a navy
senses.definition: connected with a country's navy, the branch of its armed forces that fights at sea
senses.definitionCN: 与一个国家的海军相关，即其武装力量中在海上作战的军种
senses.example: The country expanded its naval forces last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家去年扩充了海军部队。
senses.why: The Latin adjective navalis meant of ships, and since a fleet is made of ships, the word naturally names the service that operates them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词 navalis 意为「船的」，而舰队由船组成，这个词自然就用来指操纵船舰的军种。

senses.title: Of warships and their equipment
senses.definition: used of ships built for war and the bases, yards or equipment that serve them
senses.definitionCN: 用于为作战建造的舰船，以及为其服务的基地、船厂或装备
senses.example: The yard repairs naval vessels from several countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家船厂修理来自几个国家的海军舰艇。
senses.why: If navalis belongs to ships, it can describe the ships themselves, so a naval vessel is simply a ship built for war.
senses.whyCN: 既然 navalis 属于船，它也能形容船本身，所以 naval vessel 就是为战争建造的舰船。

senses.title: Connected with war at sea
senses.definition: describing battles, strategy or power exercised at sea rather than on land
senses.definitionCN: 描述在海上而非陆地上进行的战斗、战略或力量
senses.example: The two powers fought a naval battle in the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在海峡打了一场海战。
senses.why: From ships and their crews the word extends to the fighting itself, so any clash decided by fleets is naval.
senses.whyCN: 词义从船舰与舰员延伸到作战本身，所以由舰队决定胜负的交锋都叫 naval。

intro.en: Naval descends from the Latin word for ship, and it keeps that narrow maritime meaning in modern English.
intro.cn: naval 源自拉丁语中表示「船」的词，并在现代英语里保留了这个狭窄的海上含义。

items.en: Navis was the ordinary Latin word for a ship, and it stands behind navy, navigate and naval.
items.cn: navis 是拉丁语里普通的「船」字，是 navy、navigate、naval 共同的源头。

items.en: The adjective navalis meant of a ship or of ships, and it was used of fleets and sea forces.
items.cn: 形容词 navalis 意为「船的」，用于舰队和海上力量。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective as naval, keeping the sense of ships and the sea.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 naval，保留船与海的含义。

items.en: Middle English used naval for things belonging to ships, especially warships.
items.cn: 中古英语用 naval 指属于船的事物，尤指战舰。

items.en: Modern English limits naval to the navy and sea warfare, while navy names the force itself.
items.cn: 现代英语把 naval 限定在海军与海战，而 navy 指这支力量本身。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same ship stem and a near-homophone with another origin; the near-meaning group collects sea and service terms.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「船」词干上的词，以及一个来源不同的同音词；近义组收海洋与军种词汇。

entries.definition: A country's sea force, with its ships and crews.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家的海上军事力量及其舰船、舰员；海军。

entries.definition: The small hollow in the middle of the belly; it only sounds like naval, and the root is Germanic.
entries.definitionCN: 腹部中央的小凹陷，即肚脐；与 naval 只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To work out a course and steer a ship or other craft along it.
entries.definitionCN: 确定航线并驾驶船只或其他载具沿之航行。

entries.definition: Connected with the sea, shipping or sea trade.
entries.definitionCN: 与海洋、航运或海上贸易有关的。

entries.definition: Connected with ships, sailors and sailing.
entries.definitionCN: 与船、水手和航行有关的。

entries.definition: Connected with the sea, or used by a country's sea soldiers.
entries.definitionCN: 与海洋有关的，或指一国海上作战部队的。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for ship, its adjective, and English words that keep the same maritime root.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示「船」的名词、它的形容词，以及共享同一海上词根的英语词共同支撑。

normal.en: Navis is Latin for ship, so every word in this family keeps a trace of a hull on water.
normal.cn: navis 是拉丁语的「船」，这一族词都留着水面上船身的影子。

normal.en: Navy is the force, naval is the adjective that describes it, just as army and military divide the work.
normal.cn: navy 是这支力量，naval 是描述它的形容词，就像 army 与 military 的分工。

normal.en: Navigate joins navis with agere, to drive, so it literally means to drive a ship.
normal.cn: navigate 把 navis 与 agere（驾驶）合起来，字面就是「驾驶船」。

normal.en: Navel sounds the same as naval but belongs to a Germanic root for the belly, so keep the two apart.
normal.cn: navel 与 naval 读音相同，却来自表示腹部的日耳曼词根，要把两个词分开。

normal.en: Naval battle, naval base and naval officer all fix the word to the sea service, not to ships in general.
normal.cn: naval battle、naval base 与 naval officer 都把词固定在海上军种，而不是泛指船。

abstract.en: A word for ship is also the word for a nation's reach across water: the hull becomes a border.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「船」的词也成了国家跨海而去的触角：船身变成了边界。

abstract.en: Naval power is measured less by ships than by the sea lanes a fleet can keep open.
abstract.cn: 衡量海上力量，与其说看舰船数量，不如说看一支舰队能守住多少航道。

abstract.en: Keeping naval and navel apart is a small reminder that sound and sense travel on different roads.
abstract.cn: 把 naval 与 navel 分开，是一个小提醒：读音与意义走的是不同的路。

examples.en: The naval base sits on a headland above the harbour.
examples.cn: 海军基地位于港口上方的海岬。

examples.en: She served as a naval officer for ten years.
examples.cn: 她当了十年海军军官。

examples.en: The fleet won a decisive naval battle in the strait.
examples.cn: 舰队在海峡赢得了一场决定性的海战。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内我」——舰船从内港开出去，内我一片灰蓝；记住 naval 是海军的。

root: 拉丁语 navis（船）→ navalis（船的）→ 古法语 naval → 中古英语 naval；与 navel（肚脐）只是读音相近，词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is belonging to ships; from it the word narrows onto the navy, its warships and the fighting they do.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「属于船」；由此收窄到海军、海军舰艇以及它们进行的海战。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bow of a grey warship cutting the swell while sailors salute on deck.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰色军舰的舰首切开浪头，甲板上一排水兵敬礼。

branches.en: a row of grey hulls waiting inside a harbour wall
branches.cn: 一排灰色舰身停在港墙之内

branches.en: sailors standing in line for inspection on a deck
branches.cn: 水兵在甲板上列队接受检阅

branches.en: a dry dock holding a warship out of the water
branches.cn: 干船坞里被托出水面的战舰

branches.en: smoke over a strait after a night engagement
branches.cn: 夜间交战后海峡上空的硝烟

branches.en: a map marked with sea lanes a fleet must hold
branches.cn: 标着舰队必须守住航道的地图

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin noun for ship, its adjective form and an English adjective ending, with related words that keep the same root.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示「船」的名词、它的形容词形式和英语形容词词尾构成，并有共享同一词根的关联词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

latinEntries.meaning: to sail, to steer a ship

definition_en: the act of getting rid of something, or the right to use something as you wish
core_image: 垃圾车把一桶东西倒进车厢，桶底朝天
scene: 垃圾车把桶举起来，桶底朝天倒了个干净。 The safe disposal of waste costs the city a fortune.
sceneCN: 这里 disposal 指「处理」（第 1 个义项：把废弃物处理掉）；句意是安全处理垃圾花了这座城市一大笔钱。

senses.title: The act of getting rid of something
senses.definition: the act of throwing away or dealing with something unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 把不要的东西扔掉或加以处置的行为
senses.example: The disposal of waste costs money.
senses.exampleCN: 处理垃圾要花钱。
senses.why: A bin lifted upside down ends a long story.
senses.whyCN: 一只桶被倒过来，一段长故事就结束了。

senses.title: The right to use something
senses.definition: the power to use or decide about something
senses.definitionCN: 使用或决定某事的权力
senses.example: The car is at your disposal.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车随你使用。
senses.why: What you may command is what has been placed in your hand.
senses.whyCN: 你能支配的，是放进你手里的东西。

intro.en: Disposal is dispose plus -al, and dispose comes from Latin disponere, to set out in order.
intro.cn: disposal 是 dispose 加 -al；dispose 源自拉丁语 disponere（分置、安排）。

items.en: Ponere meant to place or to put down.
items.cn: ponere 指放置、放下。

items.en: Disponere meant to set things out in their places.
items.cn: disponere 指把东西各自摆好。

items.en: Disposer meant to arrange or to settle a matter.
items.cn: 古法语 disposer 指安排或了结事情。

items.en: English dispose meant to arrange and later to get rid of.
items.cn: 英语 dispose 先指安排，后指处理掉。

items.en: Disposal now names both the act and the power to use.
items.cn: 今天 disposal 既指处理行为，也指使用权。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dispose stem, and the meaning group names other forms of control.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dispose 词干，近义组列出别的处置与控制。

entries.definition: to get rid of something
made to be thrown away after use
willing or arranged in a way
the act of taking something away
the way something is dealt with
the power to decide about something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a bin turned upside down and end with a hand holding a key.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被倒过来的垃圾桶开始，落到一只握着钥匙的手。

normal.en: Dis- plus posal: things are set apart and cleared.
normal.cn: dis 加 posal，把东西分开摆好再清走。

normal.en: Waste disposal is the quiet work behind a clean street.
normal.cn: 垃圾处理是干净街道背后的安静功夫。

normal.en: At your disposal means the thing is placed in your hand.
normal.cn: 供你支配，意思是东西已放进你手里。

normal.en: A disposal site is where a city hides its leftovers.
normal.cn: 处理场是一座城藏剩饭剩菜的地方。

normal.en: The safest disposal is often the slowest one.
normal.cn: 最安全的处理，往往是最慢的那种。

abstract.en: Picture a bin lifted above the truck.
abstract.cn: 想象一只桶被举到车斗上方。

abstract.en: Picture a lid falling shut on an empty can.
abstract.cn: 想象盖子落在空罐上。

abstract.en: Picture a key laid on a table by its owner.
abstract.cn: 想象主人把钥匙放在桌上。

examples.en: The safe disposal of waste costs the city a fortune.
examples.cn: 安全处理垃圾花了这座城市一大笔钱。

examples.en: The whole library is at your disposal.
examples.cn: 整个图书馆都随你使用。

examples.en: Old chemicals need careful disposal.
examples.cn: 旧化学品需要小心处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disposal 记成「摆开处理」：dis 是分开放，pos 是放置，-al 是行为；把东西分开摆好再清掉，就是处理。

root: 由动词 dispose 加名词后缀 -al 构成；dispose 源自拉丁语 disponere（分置、安排），由 dis-（分开）与 ponere（放置）组成。本义是把东西分开摆好，后来引申为处理掉不要的东西，也指把某物交到别人手里任其支配。

sensesIntro.en: From setting things in their places to handing the key to someone else.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把东西各就各位，到把钥匙交到别人手里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bin lifted and turned upside down above a truck.
core.cn: 核心意象：垃圾桶被举起，在车斗上方倒过来。

branches.en: The first sense is the clearing away of what is unwanted.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把不要的东西清走。

branches.en: The second sense is the power left in your hand.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是留在你手里的那份权力。

branches.en: Both senses start from things placed in order.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从东西被摆放整齐开始。

branches.en: Both appear in the phrase at your disposal.
branches.cn: 两个义项都能读进「供你支配」这句话。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be handed over.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能被交出去。

intro.en: Disposal belongs to the Latin ponere family, where placing and arranging share one stem.
intro.cn: disposal 属于拉丁语 ponere 一族，放置与安排共用同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere, to place, gives disponere and dispose; -al turns the arranging into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere（放置）给出 disponere 与 dispose；后缀 -al 把安排变成名词。

items.example: Waste disposal is a city duty.
