definition_en: to jump suddenly, to jump over something, or to increase sharply
core_image: 一个人屈膝蓄力，整个人腾空越过一道窄沟
scene: 河岸边的鹿受到惊吓，前腿一蹬便越过灌木。 The deer leaped over the low hedge.
sceneCN: 这里是「跃过」（第 2 个义项：动词，指跳过某个障碍）；句意为鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。图中可辨识物件：河岸、受惊的鹿、低矮树篱。

derivatives.zh: 由 leap 与 frog 复合，义为「跳背游戏；蛙跳式超越」
由 leap 加 -er 构成，义为「跳跃者」
由 leap 加 -ing 构成，义为「跳跃的；跃动的」

senses.title: To jump suddenly
senses.definition: to move through the air by pushing off the ground with the legs
senses.definitionCN: 用腿蹬地、身体腾空移动
senses.example: The deer leaped over the low hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。
senses.why: Leap is an old Germanic verb for a springing movement, stronger and more sudden than the everyday jump.
senses.whyCN: leap 是古老的日耳曼动词，表示弹跳式的动作，比日常的 jump 更用力、更突然。

senses.title: To jump over an obstacle
senses.definition: to cross something by jumping over it
senses.definitionCN: 通过跳过去而越过某物
senses.example: He leaped the fence and ran into the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他跃过栅栏，跑进田里。
senses.why: Once the verb names the jump, the thing jumped over can become its direct object, so leap gains the sense of clearing an obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然表示跳，被跳过的东西就能作宾语，于是 leap 有了「越过障碍」的意思。

senses.title: To increase sharply
senses.definition: to rise suddenly and by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 突然且大幅度地上升
senses.example: Profits leaped in the second quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第二季度利润猛涨。
senses.why: A sharp rise looks like a jump on a graph, so the physical leap is borrowed for numbers that suddenly go up.
senses.whyCN: 陡升在图表上就像一次跳跃，于是身体的 leap 被借来形容数字的猛涨。

senses.title: A jump or a sharp rise
senses.definition: an act of jumping, or a sudden large increase
senses.definitionCN: 一次跳跃，或突然的大幅增长
senses.example: There was a leap in demand for electric cars.
senses.exampleCN: 电动汽车的需求出现了一次跃升。
senses.why: The noun simply names the event that the verb describes, whether in space or on a chart.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是给动词所描述的事件命名，无论在空间里还是在图表上。

intro.en: Leap is an Old English verb of springing, shared across the Germanic languages and unchanged in its central sense.
intro.cn: leap 是古英语中表示弹跳的动词，在日耳曼语族中广泛共享，核心义一直未变。

items.en: Hleapan meant to jump or spring, often with the image of pushing off the ground.
items.cn: hleapan 意为跳跃、弹起，常带有蹬地发力的画面。

items.en: The reconstructed *hlaupan is shared by German laufen, which shifted towards running.
items.cn: 重构形式 *hlaupan 为德语 laufen 所共享，后者词义转向「跑」。

items.en: Middle English lepen keeps the jump and adds the sense of jumping over something.
items.cn: 中古英语 lepen 保留跳跃义，并添上「跳过某物」的意思。

items.en: The figurative sense of a sudden rise appears in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 表示「突然上升」的比喻义在十七世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps both past forms, leaped and leapt, and uses leap year for the calendar's extra day.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 leaped 与 leapt 两种过去式，并用 leap year 指日历中多出的那一天。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and forms of leap; the near-meaning group gathers words for jumping and rising.
note.cn: 形近组收 leap 的复合词与变形；近义组收表示跳跃与上升的词。

normalIntro.en: A short Germanic verb with two past forms, leap keeps its spring in space and lends it to numbers.
normalIntro.cn: 一个简短的日耳曼动词带有两种过去式，leap 把弹跳留在空间里，又借给数字。

normal.en: Leap has two past forms: leaped and leapt.
normal.cn: leap 有两种过去式：leaped 与 leapt。

normal.en: Leap over is the phrase for clearing an obstacle.
normal.cn: leap over 是表示越过障碍的搭配。

normal.en: Leap year takes its name from the extra day that makes the calendar jump.
normal.cn: leap year 得名于让日历「跳」一下的多余那一天。

normal.en: Leapfrog joins leap and frog, from a game of jumping over backs.
normal.cn: leapfrog 由 leap 与 frog 组合，来自跳过别人背部的游戏。

normal.en: Leap to conclusions means deciding without enough evidence.
normal.cn: leap to conclusions 意为没有足够证据就下结论。

abstract.en: A jump needs a firm push before it needs open air, which is why leap implies stored force.
abstract.cn: 跳跃先需要稳稳蹬地，才需要腾空，所以 leap 含着蓄力。

abstract.en: The same word describes a deer and a profit because both leave the ground suddenly.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能描述鹿，也能描述利润，因为二者都突然离开了原来的水平。

abstract.en: In a leap, the body is briefly between two places, belonging to neither.
abstract.cn: 在跳跃中，身体短暂处在两地之间，谁也不属于。

examples.en: The deer leaped over the low hedge.
examples.cn: 鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。

examples.en: Profits leaped in the second quarter.
examples.cn: 第二季度利润猛涨。

examples.en: There was a leap in demand for electric cars.
examples.cn: 电动汽车的需求出现了一次跃升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「力扑」——用力扑出去，就是 leap。

root: 古英语 hleapan（跳跃），与德语 laufen 同出日耳曼语族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a springing push-off; it extends from a jump to clearing an obstacle, then to a sharp rise and the increase itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是蹬地弹起；由跳跃扩展到越过障碍，再扩展到猛涨与那次增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body folded at the knees, then flying clear over a narrow ditch.
core.cn: 核心意象：屈膝蓄力，整个人腾空越过一道窄沟。

branches.en: a deer lifting off the bank

branches.en: a runner clearing a low fence

branches.en: a line on a graph bending upward
branches.cn: 图表上陡然上弯的线

branches.en: a single step up that changes the level
branches.cn: 改变水平的一级台阶

branches.cn: 同一次发力，一次越过栅栏，一次越过去年的数字

definition_en: a statement saying that someone has done something wrong
core_image: 一根手指直直指向对面的人
scene: 他声音平静，否认了那项指控。 He denied the accusation with a calm voice.
sceneCN: 这里的 accusation 是「指控」（第 1 个义项：正式说某人有错）；句意是他平静地否认了指控。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「指控；指责」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「被指控的」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「指控者」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「指责的」

senses.title: A formal charge against someone
senses.definition: a public statement that a person has committed a crime or a serious fault
senses.definitionCN: 公开指出某人犯了罪或有严重过失的话
senses.example: The accusation was read aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 那项指控在法庭上被大声宣读。
senses.why: The Latin causa means a lawsuit, so the noun began as the act of bringing a case rather than a private complaint.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 causa 意为「诉讼」，所以这个名词最初指把案子提上法庭的行为，而不是私下的抱怨。

senses.title: The charge itself
senses.definition: the particular wrong that someone is said to have done
senses.definitionCN: 某人被说成做过的那件具体的错事
senses.example: The accusation against him was theft.
senses.exampleCN: 对他的指控是盗窃。
senses.why: Once a case is opened, the word shifts from the act of charging to the content of the charge, the thing written in the file.
senses.whyCN: 案子一立，词义就从「提出指控」转到「指控的内容」，也就是写进卷宗的那一条。

senses.title: An informal charge of blame
senses.definition: a claim of blame made outside any court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭之外提出的责备性说法
senses.example: Her accusation hurt him more than the fine.
senses.exampleCN: 她的指责比罚款更伤他。
senses.why: A lawsuit can shrink to a quarrel; the same pointing finger now appears at the dinner table rather than the dock.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼可以缩成一场争吵；同一根指点的手指，如今出现在餐桌边，而不是被告席前。

intro.en: The noun comes from the Latin verb for bringing a case, built on the word for a lawsuit.
intro.cn: 这个名词来自拉丁语中「提起诉讼」的动词，其词根是「诉讼」。

items.cn: accusare 意为在法庭上追究某人。

同根名词，义为「空洞；无内容」
同根形容词，义为「空的；空缺的」

senses.title: A space with no air or matter
senses.definition: an enclosed space from which air and other matter have been removed
senses.definitionCN: 被抽去空气与其他物质的封闭空间
senses.example: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
senses.exampleCN: 声音无法在真空中传播。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant an empty space, and physics simply kept that exact meaning for a space with nothing in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本指空旷之处，物理学只是原样保留了这一含义，用来指里面什么都没有的空间。

senses.title: A machine that cleans by suction
senses.definition: an electrical machine that removes dust by sucking air through it
senses.definitionCN: 用抽气的方式把灰尘吸走的电器
senses.example: She ran the vacuum over the carpet twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她用吸尘器把地毯吸了两遍。
senses.why: A cleaner that works by creating a partial vacuum took the name of the emptiness it makes.
senses.whyCN: 一种靠制造局部真空来清扫的机器，干脆用它所造出的「空」来命名。

senses.title: An empty gap left by something missing
senses.definition: a state or place left empty after something important is lost
senses.definitionCN: 重要之物失去后留下的空荡状态或位置
senses.example: Retirement left a vacuum in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 退休在团队里留下了一片空白。
senses.why: If an empty space is the point, then a team missing its leader is an empty space too, and the metaphor needs no change of word.
senses.whyCN: 既然关键在「空出来的位置」，那么失去领头人的团队也是一处空位，比喻连词都不用换。

senses.title: To clean with a suction machine
senses.definition: to clean a floor or a surface with a vacuum cleaner
senses.definitionCN: 用吸尘器清洁地面或表面
senses.example: He vacuums the stairs every Saturday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每周六早上用吸尘器吸楼梯。
senses.why: The noun naming the machine turns into a verb once people start doing the job with it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们用这台机器干活，称呼机器的名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: In isolation from real conditions
senses.definition: in the phrase in a vacuum, meaning without any surrounding influence or context
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in a vacuum，指没有任何周围影响或情境
senses.example: No plan is made in a vacuum; every room has a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 任何计划都不是凭空定下的，每间屋子都有预算。
senses.why: A physical vacuum has no surroundings at all, and thinking with no surroundings borrowed the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 物理真空周围什么也没有，没有周围环境可言的思考便借用了同一幅画面。

intro.en: A Latin noun of emptiness borrowed whole; physics, the home, and the office each took it over.
intro.cn: 一个整体借入的拉丁语「空」名词；物理学、家务与办公室各自把它拿去用了。

items.en: Vacuum was the neuter of vacuus, empty, and meant an empty space.
items.cn: vacuum 是 vacuus（空的）的中性形式，意为空旷之处。

items.en: Writers on natural philosophy used the word for a space with no air in it.
items.cn: 自然哲学的作者用这个词指其中没有空气的空间。

items.en: English takes the word over in the sixteenth century, at first for that physical sense.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪接收这个词，最初用于这层物理含义。

items.en: The suction cleaner of the early twentieth century borrows the name.
items.cn: 二十世纪早期的吸尘器借用了这个名字。

items.en: The figurative sense of a missing leader or of context-free thinking follows in modern usage.
items.cn: 失去领导者或脱离情境思考的引申义，在现代用法中随之出现。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the vac- family of emptiness, and the near-meaning group gives the empty and the full.
note.cn: 形近组收集表示「空」的 vac- 词族，近义组则给出空与满。

entries.definition: showing no thought
empty, not occupied
emptiness of mind or substance
amount of space, only the ending is close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 体积；只是词尾相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a completely empty space
an unfilled space
the state of having nothing inside
the state of being full

normalIntro.en: The word was borrowed whole from Latin as an emptied space; every later sense keeps that picture of nothing inside.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词整体借自拉丁语，是「空掉的空间」；此后每个义项都保留「里面什么都没有」的画面。

normal.en: The plural is vacuums in ordinary use and vacua in physics writing.
normal.cn: 日常复数写 vacuums，物理文字里则用 vacua。

normal.en: In a vacuum is the fixed phrase for acting without context.
normal.cn: in a vacuum 是「脱离情境」的固定说法。

normal.en: Vacuum cleaner is often shortened to vacuum, and then turned into a verb.
normal.cn: vacuum cleaner 常简称为 vacuum，再转成动词。

normal.en: A power vacuum appears when a weak government leaves a gap.
normal.cn: 权力真空出现在弱政府留下的空缺里。

normal.en: Vacuum shares its root with vacant and vacation.
normal.cn: vacuum 与 vacant、vacation 同根。

abstract.en: Picture a glass bell with a pipe on top, pulling the air out.
abstract.cn: 想象带抽气管的玻璃罩把空气抽走。

abstract.en: Hear the whistle of an old vacuum cleaner on a Sunday morning.
abstract.cn: 听周日早晨旧吸尘器的啸叫声。

abstract.en: See an empty desk where an old colleague used to sit.
abstract.cn: 看老同事曾坐过的那张空桌。

examples.en: The experiment took place in a vacuum, so there was no air resistance.
examples.cn: 这项实验在真空中进行，因此没有空气阻力。

examples.en: He vacuums the flat every Sunday.
examples.cn: 他每个周日都用吸尘器打扫公寓。

examples.en: The sudden resignation created a vacuum at the top of the firm.
examples.cn: 突然辞职在公司顶层造成了一片真空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖空」——把里面的空气挖空了，就是真空。

root: 拉丁语 vacuus（空的）的中性名词形式 vacuum（空旷之处），整体借入英语；同根有 vacare（空着）

sensesIntro.en: One sealed empty space gives the physics sense, the suction machine, the gap left by a person, the verb of cleaning, and thought cut off from context.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个封闭的空空间给出物理义、抽气机器、失人留下的空缺、清扫动作，以及脱离情境的思考。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass bell emptied until feather and coin fall together.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃罩被抽空，羽毛与硬币一同落下。

branches.en: The lab branch: air removed so nothing slows the fall.
branches.cn: 实验室分支：空气被抽走，没有东西拖慢下落。

branches.en: The household branch: a machine that sucks dust.
branches.cn: 家务分支：吸走灰尘的机器。

branches.en: The gap branch: something important is missing.
branches.cn: 空缺分支：重要的东西不见了。

branches.en: The verb branch: running that machine over a floor.
branches.cn: 动词分支：用那台机器走过地面。

branches.en: The isolation branch: no surrounding influence at all.
branches.cn: 孤立分支：周围没有任何影响。

intro.en: A Latin noun taken over complete, so the Latin ending is still visible at the end.
intro.cn: 一个整体借入的拉丁名词，末尾的拉丁词尾至今清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: The root vacu- means empty in Latin; vacuus is the adjective and the neuter noun vacuum was borrowed unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 vacu- 意为空的；vacuus 是形容词，中性名词 vacuum 则原样借入英语。

items.example: The root carries the whole meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载全部意义。

items.example: Vacuum is a Latin neuter noun.
items.exampleCN: vacuum 是拉丁语中性名词。
vacant 留在日常的房间上。

items.example: Vacation moved to the idea of free days.
items.exampleCN: vacation 转向空闲日子的概念。

items.example: Cleaner is the tool part of the compound.
items.exampleCN: cleaner 是复合词里的工具部分。
flask 出现在 vacuum flask 中。

definition_zh: 相互作用；互相影响；互动
definition_en: to act on each other, or to talk and do things together with other people
core_image: 两个人对着同一个屏幕，你按一下，他回应一句
scene: 小区广场上几个孩子轮流推着同一个球，谁推出去谁就笑着跑开。 Some medicines interact badly with coffee.
sceneCN: 这里 interact 是「相互作用、互相配合」（第 1 个义项：彼此产生影响），句意有些药与咖啡同用会产生不良反应。画面里的物件：传着的球、笑声、药盒与咖啡杯。

pos.zh: 动词：相互作用；互相影响；互动

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「相互作用；互动」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「互动的」
由 interactive 加 -ly 构成，义为「互动地」
由本词去前缀构成，义为「反应」

senses.title: Things acting on each other
senses.definition: to have an effect on each other, as substances, forces, or systems do
senses.definitionCN: 像物质、力或系统那样彼此产生影响
senses.example: The two chemicals interact only when heated.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种化学品只在加热时才相互作用。
senses.why: Inter- means between, agere means to do; together they describe mutual action.
senses.whyCN: inter- 意为「在之间」，agere 意为「做」，合起来即相互的动作。

senses.title: People dealing with people
senses.definition: to talk, work, or play with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人交谈、共事或一起玩
senses.example: The children learn to interact before they learn to read.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们先学会相处，再学会阅读。
senses.why: Social life is modelled as actions exchanged between persons.
senses.whyCN: 社交生活被看作人与人之间交换的动作。

senses.title: Users and machines
senses.definition: to use a device or program, giving it instructions and receiving responses
senses.definitionCN: 使用装置或程序，给出指令并收到回应
senses.example: Visitors can interact with the map by touching any district.
senses.exampleCN: 访客可以触碰任一区域来与地图互动。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word for the back-and-forth between people and machines.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借这个词形容人与机器之间的往来。

intro.en: Interact joins Latin inter- "between" to agere "to do", a verb English borrowed from react.
intro.cn: interact 把拉丁语 inter-「在……之间」接到 agere「做」上，而英语是借 react 而造出它的。

items.en: Agere means to drive, do, or act, and yields actus and actio.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、做、行动，生出 actus 与 actio。

items.en: Inter as a preposition meant between, among, or mutually.
items.cn: inter 作介词意为「在……之间、互相」。

items.en: React appeared first; interact was coined in the early nineteenth century on its pattern.
items.cn: 先有 react，interact 在十九世纪初按它的样子造出。

items.en: Scientists used it for forces and substances acting mutually.
items.cn: 科学家用它指力与物质的相互作用。

items.en: Social science and computing made it the ordinary word for people and screens.
items.cn: 社会科学与计算机让它成为形容人与屏幕的日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the agere root of doing; the near-meaning group holds other words for mutual contact.
note.cn: 形近组共享「做」这一词根 agere；近义组收表示相互接触的词。

entries.definition: To act back when something happens to you.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「反应」，对发生的事情作出回应。

entries.definition: A business deal, an acting across between two parties.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交易」，双方之间完成的一次业务。

entries.definition: To do something, or a deed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「行动」，名词义为「行为」。

entries.definition: To pass information or feeling to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「沟通」，传递信息或感受。

entries.definition: To work with others towards one aim.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「合作」，为同一目标共同努力。

entries.definition: To mix freely in a crowd.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「交际」，在人群中自由往来。

normalIntro.en: The hooks split the word into inter- and act and follow where it is actually used.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词拆成 inter- 与 act，并沿着它实际使用的场合走。

normal.en: Inter plus act: doing between, back and forth.
normal.cn: inter 加 act：在双方之间来回地做。

normal.en: Two medicines may interact; two friends certainly will.
normal.cn: 两种药会相互作用；两个朋友更是一定会。

normal.en: Children interact with toys before they speak perfectly.
normal.cn: 孩子说话还不流利时就会与玩具互动。

normal.en: Users interact with the map by tapping.
normal.cn: 用户靠轻触与地图互动。

normal.en: React is to act back; interact is to act together.
normal.cn: react 是回身反应，interact 是彼此一起动。

abstract.en: Nothing stands alone: everything interacts.
abstract.cn: 没有东西独自立着，万物都在相互作用。

abstract.en: Characters in a story are known by how they interact.
abstract.cn: 故事里的人物靠彼此往来而被认出来。

abstract.en: The word marks the space between two doings.
abstract.cn: 这个词标出两件事之间的那段空间。

examples.en: These drugs interact with each other and must not be mixed.
examples.cn: 这些药会相互作用，不能混用。

examples.en: Pupils interact with visiting speakers in small groups.
examples.cn: 学生们以小组形式与来访的讲者互动。

examples.en: The child had hardly interacted with anyone all term.
examples.cn: 这孩子整个学期几乎没和任何人来往。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特爱克」——网络特长爱互相切磋，就是互动

root: 拉丁语 inter-「在……之间」+ agere「做、驱动」→ 英语先有 react，再按此模式造出 interact。同族：interaction、react、act。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: mutual action of things, social dealings, and using a device.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：事物的相互作用、人际往来，以及使用装置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people pushing one ball back and forth.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人来回推同一个球。

branches.en: THE TWO CHEMICALS: heat makes them act on each other.
branches.cn: 两种化学品这条线：加热使它们相互起作用。

branches.en: THE PLAYGROUND: play is an exchange of actions.
branches.cn: 操场这条线：游戏就是动作的交换。

branches.en: THE TOUCH SCREEN: a tap brings a reply.
branches.cn: 触屏这条线：一触得到回应。

branches.en: THE LINK: mutual action applies to bodies and to people.
branches.cn: 连接线：相互动作既用于物体也用于人。

branches.en: THE LINK: machines are treated as social partners.
branches.cn: 连接线：机器被当作社交对象。

intro.en: Interact = inter- "between" + act, from Latin agere "to do".
intro.cn: interact = inter-「在……之间」+ act（来自拉丁语 agere「做」）。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter and agere are both recorded; the English compound is modern.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 与 agere 均有记载，英语的合成词则是近代产物。

items.example: From agere, the root of many words.
items.exampleCN: 来自 agere，许多词共同的根。

items.example: The -ent of agere is visible here.
items.exampleCN: agere 的 -ent 在这里可见。

items.example: A plural of the same Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 同一拉丁词干的复数形式。

definition_en: the power believed to control events, what happens to someone or something, or death and ruin in literary use
core_image: 旧剧院门口的告示牌在风里摇晃，人们等待它最后的决定
scene: 这座老剧院最终会怎样，还没有人知道。 The fate of the old theater is still unknown.
sceneCN: 这里 fate 是「结局；遭遇」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这座老剧院的命运仍不清楚。

senses.title: The power that decides events
senses.definition: the power believed to control what happens
senses.definitionCN: 被认为控制事件发生的力量
senses.example: He blamed fate for his bad luck.
senses.exampleCN: 他把坏运气归咎于命运。
senses.why: The core sense is an unseen controlling power.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是看不见的主宰力量。

senses.title: What happens to someone
senses.definition: the things that happen to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 发生在某人或某物身上的事
senses.example: The fate of the old theater is still unknown.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老剧院的命运仍不清楚。
senses.why: The general power narrows to a particular outcome.
senses.whyCN: 笼统的力量缩小为具体结局。

senses.title: Death or destruction
senses.definition: death or ruin, especially in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 尤用于文学中的死亡或毁灭
senses.example: The sailors met their fate at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们在海上遇难。
senses.why: The outcome sense becomes a euphemism for death.
senses.whyCN: 结局义成为死亡的委婉说法。

intro.en: Fate comes from Latin fatum, something spoken, and so a divine decree.
intro.cn: fate 源自拉丁语 fatum（说出的话），因此指神谕或天命。

items.en: Fari meant to speak.
items.cn: fari 意为说话。

items.en: Fatum meant a spoken decree or destiny.
items.cn: fatum 意为说出的神谕或命运。

items.en: Fate meant the power that decides events.
items.cn: fate 意为主宰事件的力量。

items.en: Fate also named what happens to a person.
items.cn: fate 也开始指发生在某人身上的事。

items.en: Fate can also mean death or ruin in literary use.
items.cn: 现代文学用法中 fate 还可指死亡或毁灭。

note.en: Fate is compared with similar short words and with words for destiny and doom.
note.cn: 把 fate 与形近短词以及表示命运和厄运的词作比较。

entries.definition: grease stored in the body
a door in a wall or fence
arriving after the expected time
the events that will happen to a person
chance or luck in life
a terrible future that cannot be avoided

normalIntro.en: Fate is the power behind events, and fatal describes its deadly result.
normalIntro.cn: fate 是事件背后的力量，fatal 描述它致命的结果。

normal.en: Fate is the power behind events.
normal.cn: fate 是事件背后的力量。

normal.en: A twist of fate changes a life.
normal.cn: 命运的转折会改变人生。

normal.en: Fated means decided in advance.
normal.cn: fated 意为预先注定的。

normal.en: Fatal means leading to death.
normal.cn: fatal 意为导致死亡的。

normal.en: Fateful means having great consequences.
normal.cn: fateful 意为影响重大的。

abstract.en: Fate is the spoken decree behind events.
abstract.cn: 命运就是事件背后被说出的神谕。

abstract.en: Destiny and fate both name what seems beyond choice.
abstract.cn: destiny 与 fate 都指看似无法选择的事。

abstract.en: The word carries both comfort and fear.
abstract.cn: 这个词既带来安慰，也带来恐惧。

examples.en: The two friends shared the same fate.
examples.cn: 这两个朋友遭遇了同样的命运。

examples.en: A twist of fate brought them together.
examples.cn: 命运的转折让他们走到一起。

examples.en: She refused to accept her fate.
examples.cn: 她拒绝接受自己的命运。

dict_mnemonic.text: fate 源自拉丁语 fatum（说出的话、神谕），命运被看作被说出并决定的结局。

root: 源自拉丁语 fatum（说出的话、神谕、命运），来自 fari（说）。

sensesIntro.en: Fate means the power that controls events, what happens to someone, or death and ruin.
sensesIntro.cn: fate 意为主宰事件的力量、某人的结局，或死亡毁灭。

core.en: A power or outcome that seems beyond choice.
core.cn: 看似无法选择的支配力量或结局。

branches.en: An unseen power controlling events.
branches.cn: 控制事件的看不见的力量。

branches.en: The outcome waiting for a person or thing.
branches.cn: 等待某人或某物的结局。

branches.en: Death or ruin as a final outcome.
branches.cn: 作为最终结局的死亡或毁灭。

branches.en: The power and its result are two sides of one idea.
branches.cn: 力量与其结果是同一个概念的两面。

branches.en: A final outcome can mean death.
branches.cn: 最终结局可以意味着死亡。

intro.en: Fate forms adjectives and nouns about destiny and death.
intro.cn: fate 构成表示命运与死亡的形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fatum and fari, to speak, are the sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fatum 与 fari（说）是词源。

items.exampleCN: 这个决定产生了重大后果。
那艘倒霉的船再也没有回来。
